title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第四十三 梁武帝諸子
title.en: Volume 53 Biographies 43: Sons of Emperor Wu of Liang
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第四十三 梁武帝諸子 Volume 53 Biographies 43: Sons of Emperor Wu of Liang

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十三

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Forty-Three
translations.idiomatic: Biography 43

sentences.zh: 梁武帝諸子

translations.literal: The Various Sons of Emperor Wu of Liang
translations.idiomatic: The Sons of Emperor Wu of Liang

sentences.zh: 武帝八男。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had eight sons.

sentences.zh: 丁貴嬪生昭明太子統、簡文皇帝、廬陵威王續。

translations.literal: Noble Consort Ding bore Crown Prince Zhaoming Tong, Emperor Jianwen, and Prince Wei of Luling Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Noble Consort Ding gave birth to Crown Prince Zhaoming (Tong), Emperor Jianwen, and Prince Wei of Luling (Xu).

sentences.zh: 阮修容生孝元皇帝。

translations.literal: Lady Ruan bore Emperor Xiaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ruan gave birth to Emperor Xiaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 吳淑媛生豫章王綜。

translations.literal: Lady Wu bore Prince of Yuzhang Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu gave birth to the Prince of Yuzhang, Zong.

sentences.zh: 董昭儀生南康簡王績。

translations.literal: Lady of Bright Deportment Dong bore Prince Jian of Nankang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Bright Deportment Dong gave birth to Prince Jian of Nankang, Ji.

sentences.zh: 丁充華生邵陵攜王綸。

translations.literal: Lady Ding bore Prince Xi of Shaoling Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ding gave birth to Prince Xi of Shaoling, Lun.

sentences.zh: 葛修容生武陵王紀。

translations.literal: Lady Ge bore Prince of Wuling Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ge gave birth to the Prince of Wuling, Ji.

sentences.zh: 天監元年十一月，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Tianjian, he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Tianjian 1, he was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時年幼，依舊居於內，拜東宮官屬，文武皆入直永福省。

translations.literal: At the time he was still young and continued to reside within the inner palace as before; Eastern Palace officials were appointed, and both civil and military officers all entered duty at Yongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was still very young, so he continued to live inside the inner palace as before. Eastern Palace staff were appointed, and both civil and military attendants took their posts at Yongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 五年六月庚戌，出居東宮。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day of the sixth month of the fifth year, he moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day of the sixth month of year 5, he moved out to take up residence in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 太子生而聰叡，三歲受孝經、論語，五歲遍讀五經，悉通諷誦。

translations.literal: The crown prince was born intelligent and keen-witted; at three he received instruction in the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, and at five he read through the Five Classics and could recite them all from memory.
translations.idiomatic: From birth the crown prince was bright and perceptive. At three he began the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects; by five he had read all the Five Classics and could recite them fluently from memory.

sentences.zh: 性仁孝，自出宮，恒思戀不樂。

translations.literal: By nature he was benevolent and filial; from the time he left the inner palace, he constantly longed for home and was unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and devoted by nature, he was restless and unhappy after moving out of the inner palace, always longing to return.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，每五日一朝，多便留永福省，或五日三日乃還宮。

translations.literal: The emperor, knowing this, had him attend court every five days; often he would be kept at Yongfu Palace, or only after three or five days would he return to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, the emperor had him come to court every five days and often kept him at Yongfu Palace—sometimes for three days, sometimes for five—before he returned to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 八年九月，于壽安殿講孝經，盡通大義。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year, he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety at Shou'an Hall and fully mastered its great principles.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 8, he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in Shou'an Hall and demonstrated a thorough grasp of its essential meaning.

sentences.zh: 講畢，親臨釋奠于國學。

translations.literal: When the lecture was finished, he personally went to the National Academy to perform the sacrifice to Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: When the lecture ended, he personally went to the National Academy to offer the Confucian sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 年十二，於內省見獄官將讞事。

translations.literal: At twelve years of age, while in the inner palace he saw prison officials about to review cases.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve, while still in the inner palace, he saw court officials preparing to review criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 問左右曰：「是皁衣何為者？」

translations.literal: He asked those around him, "What are those people in dark robes doing?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked his attendants, "Who are those men in dark robes, and what are they doing?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「廷尉官屬。」

translations.literal: They replied, "Officers of the Court of Judicature."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Attendants of the minister of justice."

sentences.zh: 召視其書，曰：「是皆可念，我得判否？」

translations.literal: He summoned them to look at their documents and said, "These are all worth considering—may I pass judgment?"
translations.idiomatic: He had them bring the records over and said, "These all deserve careful thought. May I decide the cases?"

sentences.zh: 有司以統幼，紿之曰：「得。」

translations.literal: The officials, because Tong was young, deceived him, saying, "You may."
translations.idiomatic: The officials, thinking Tong was too young to understand, humored him and said, "You may."

sentences.zh: 其獄皆刑罪上，統皆署杖五十。

translations.literal: The cases were all capital offenses, yet Tong marked them all with fifty blows of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Every case involved capital crimes, yet Tong signed off on fifty strokes of the staff for each.

sentences.zh: 有司抱具獄，不知所為，具言於帝，帝笑而從之。

translations.literal: The officials, clutching the completed case files and not knowing what to do, reported everything to the emperor, who laughed and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The officials, holding the completed dossiers and unsure what to do, reported the matter fully to the emperor, who laughed and let it stand.

sentences.zh: 自是數使聽訟，每有欲寬縱者，即使太子決之。

translations.literal: From then on he was repeatedly sent to hear lawsuits; whenever there was a desire to show leniency, the crown prince was made to decide the case.
translations.idiomatic: After that he was often assigned to hear cases, and whenever the court wished to temper justice with mercy, the crown prince was put in charge of the decision.

sentences.zh: 建康縣讞誣人誘口，獄翻，縣以太子仁愛，故輕當杖四十。

translations.literal: Jiankang County tried a case of false accusation and entrapment; when the verdict was reversed, the county, because the crown prince was benevolent, therefore lightly assessed the penalty at forty blows of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: In a reversed Jiankang County case involving false accusation, the county set the punishment at only forty strokes, counting on the crown prince's compassion.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「彼若得罪，便闔家孥戮，今縱不以其罪罪之，豈可輕罰而已，可付冶十年。」

translations.literal: He ordered, "If he had been convicted, his whole family would have been executed along with him. Even though we do not punish him for the crime he did not commit, how can we merely impose a light penalty? He may be sentenced to ten years of forced labor."
translations.idiomatic: He ruled, "Had he been found guilty, his entire household would have faced execution. Even though we are not punishing him for a crime he did not commit, a light penalty is not enough—sentence him to ten years of penal servitude."

sentences.zh: 十四年正月朔旦，帝臨軒，冠太子于太極殿。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the fourteenth year, the emperor took his seat at the imperial hall and capped the crown prince in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of year 14, the emperor presided from the throne and conducted the crown prince's coming-of-age ceremony in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 舊制太子著遠遊冠、金蟬翠緌纓，至是詔加金博山。

translations.literal: By old regulation the crown prince wore the far-roaming cap with a golden cicada and green tassel cord; on this occasion an edict added a golden Mount Bo ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Under earlier rules the crown prince wore the far-roaming cap with a golden cicada and green tassel; now an edict added a golden Mount Bo crest as well.

sentences.zh: 太子美姿容，善舉止，讀書數行並下，過目皆憶。

translations.literal: The crown prince had handsome looks and graceful bearing; when he read, he took in several lines at once, and whatever he saw he remembered.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in appearance and dignified in bearing, he could read several lines at a glance and remember whatever passed before his eyes.

sentences.zh: 每游宴祖道，賦詩至十數韻，或作劇韻，皆屬思便成，無所點易。

translations.literal: Whenever he feasted or attended farewell banquets, he composed poems of ten or more rhymes, or even difficult rhyme schemes, all completed as soon as the theme was set, without a single revision.
translations.idiomatic: At banquets and farewell gatherings he would compose poems of ten or more rhymes, sometimes on demanding rhyme schemes, finishing them on the spot without changing a word.

sentences.zh: 帝大弘佛教，親自講說。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly promoted Buddhism and personally lectured on the doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor vigorously promoted Buddhism and preached the doctrine himself.

sentences.zh: 太子亦素信三寶，遍覽眾經。

translations.literal: The crown prince also had long believed in the Three Treasures and read widely among the sutras.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had long been a devout Buddhist and had read widely in the scriptures.

sentences.zh: 乃于宮內別立慧義殿，專為法集之所。

translations.literal: He then established Huiyi Hall separately within the palace, devoted exclusively to Buddhist assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace he built Huiyi Hall as a dedicated venue for Buddhist gatherings.

sentences.zh: 招引名僧，自立二諦、法身義。

translations.literal: He invited eminent monks and himself formulated doctrines on the two truths and the dharma body.
translations.idiomatic: He invited renowned monks and developed his own interpretations of the two truths and the dharma body.

sentences.zh: 普通元年四月，甘露降於慧義殿，咸以為至德所感。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Putong, sweet dew fell at Huiyi Hall, and all regarded it as a response to supreme virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Putong 1, sweet dew descended on Huiyi Hall, which everyone took as a sign of his supreme virtue.

sentences.zh: 時俗稍奢，太子欲以己率物，服御樸素，身衣浣衣，膳不兼肉。

translations.literal: Customs of the time had grown somewhat extravagant; the crown prince wished to lead others by his own example, keeping his apparel plain and simple, wearing washed clothes himself, and never serving more than one kind of meat at a meal.
translations.idiomatic: As luxury spread in society, the crown prince sought to set an example through frugality: plain dress, worn garments, and never more than one kind of meat at table.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月，始興王憺薨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year, Prince of Shixing Dan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 3, Prince of Shixing, Dan, died.

sentences.zh: 舊事以東宮禮絕傍親，書翰並依常儀。

translations.literal: By old practice, because Eastern Palace rites severed ties with collateral kin, letters and documents all followed ordinary protocol.
translations.idiomatic: By established custom, Eastern Palace protocol cut off mourning ties with collateral relatives, so correspondence followed ordinary forms.

sentences.zh: 太子以為疑，命僕劉孝綽議其事。

translations.literal: The crown prince found this doubtful and ordered Secretary Liu Xiaochuo to deliberate on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was uncertain about this and asked Secretary Liu Xiaochuo to study the question.

sentences.zh: 孝綽議曰：「案張鏡撰東宮儀記，稱'三朝發哀者，踰月不舉樂；

translations.literal: Xiaochuo deliberated, saying, "According to Zhang Jing's Eastern Palace Ceremonial Record, it states, 'For those who announce mourning on three mornings, music is not performed beyond the month;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo argued, "Zhang Jing's Eastern Palace Ceremonial Record says, 'When mourning is announced on three mornings, music is suspended for more than a month;

sentences.zh: 鼓吹寢奏，服限亦然'。

translations.literal: drums and pipes cease performance, and the period of mourning dress is the same.
translations.idiomatic: drums and pipes are silenced, and the mourning period for dress is the same.

sentences.zh: 尋傍絕之義，義在去服，服雖可奪，情豈無悲。

translations.literal: Examining the meaning of severing ties with collateral kin, the principle lies in removing mourning dress; though dress may be stripped away, can grief truly be absent?
translations.idiomatic: The rule of severing ties with collateral kin is about ending formal mourning dress—but even if the dress is removed, the grief need not disappear.

sentences.zh: 鐃歌輟奏，良亦為此。

translations.literal: The halting of cymbal songs is precisely for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: That is precisely why cymbal music is suspended.

sentences.zh: 既有悲情，宜稱兼慕，卒哭之後，依常舉樂，稱悲竟，此理例相符。

translations.literal: Since there is grief, one should use the term 'mourning together'; after the final wailing, music may be performed as usual, and when grief is declared ended, this accords with reason and precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Where grief remains, correspondence should use the phrase 'mourning together.' After the final wailing, music may resume as usual, and when grief is declared ended, reason and precedent align.

sentences.zh: 謂猶應稱兼慕，請至卒哭。」

translations.literal: It is held that one should still use the term 'mourning together,' and this is requested until the final wailing."
translations.idiomatic: He recommended continuing to use 'mourning together' until the final wailing."

sentences.zh: 僕射徐勉、左率周舍、家令陸襄並同孝綽議。

translations.literal: Vice Director Xu Mian, Left Leader Zhou She, and Household Steward Lu Xiang all agreed with Xiaochuo's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xu Mian, Left Leader Zhou She, and Household Steward Lu Xiang all sided with Xiaochuo.

sentences.zh: 太子令曰：「張鏡儀記雲，'依士禮，終服月稱慕悼'。

translations.literal: The crown prince ordered, "Zhang Jing's Ceremonial Record says, 'According to the rites of scholars, after the mourning period one uses the term mourning and lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince replied, "Zhang Jing's Ceremonial Record says, 'Under the rites of scholars, after the mourning period one writes mourning and lamentation.

sentences.zh: 又云，'凡三朝發哀者，踰月不舉樂'。

translations.literal: It also says, 'For all who announce mourning on three mornings, music is not performed beyond the month.
translations.idiomatic: It also says, 'Whenever mourning is announced on three mornings, music is suspended for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 劉僕議雲，'傍絕之義，義在去服，服雖可奪，情豈無悲。

translations.literal: Secretary Liu's deliberation says, 'The meaning of severing ties with collateral kin lies in removing mourning dress; though dress may be stripped away, can grief truly be absent?
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Liu argues, 'Severing ties with collateral kin is about ending formal mourning—but even if the dress is removed, grief need not vanish.

sentences.zh: 卒哭之後，依常舉樂，稱悲竟，此理例相符'。

translations.literal: After the final wailing, music may be performed as usual, and when grief is declared ended, this accords with reason and precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After the final wailing, music may resume as usual, and when grief is declared ended, reason and precedent align.

sentences.zh: 尋情悲之說，非止卒哭之後，緣情為論，此自難一也。

translations.literal: Examining the argument about grief, it is not limited to after the final wailing; arguing from emotion, this is itself the first difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: On the question of grief, the issue is not confined to the period after the final wailing. Arguing from emotion alone, this is the first problem.

sentences.zh: 用張鏡之'舉樂'，棄張鏡之'稱悲'。

translations.literal: To use Zhang Jing's 'perform music' while discarding Zhang Jing's 'declare grief'—
translations.idiomatic: To adopt Zhang Jing's rule on music while rejecting his rule on declaring grief—

sentences.zh: 一鏡之言，取捨有異，此自難二也。

translations.literal: from one man's words, to pick and choose differently—this is itself the second difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: picking selectively from a single authority creates a second problem.

sentences.zh: 陸家令止雲'多歷年所'，恐非事證。

translations.literal: Household Steward Lu merely says 'for many years,' which I fear is not evidence grounded in the matter itself.
translations.idiomatic: Household Steward Lu merely cites 'long-standing practice,' which is hardly solid evidence.

sentences.zh: 雖復累稔所用，意常未安。

translations.literal: Even though it has been used for many accumulated years, in my mind I have never been at ease with it.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the practice has stood for years, I have never been comfortable with it.

sentences.zh: 近亦嘗以此問外，由來立意，謂猶應有慕悼之言。

translations.literal: Recently I also raised this question elsewhere; from the outset my intent has been that there should still be language of mourning and lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: I recently raised this question with others as well. From the start my view has been that correspondence should still include language of mourning and lamentation.

sentences.zh: 張豈不知舉樂為大，稱悲事小。

translations.literal: Could Zhang have been unaware that performing music is a great matter and declaring grief a small one?
translations.idiomatic: Surely Zhang knew that resuming music was the weightier issue and declaring grief the lesser one.

sentences.zh: 所以用小而忽大，良亦有以。

translations.literal: The reason he used the small and neglected the great surely also had its grounds.
translations.idiomatic: His reason for treating the lesser matter seriously while setting aside the greater one must have had its logic.

sentences.zh: 至如元正六佾，事為國章，雖情或未安，而禮不可廢。

translations.literal: As for the six rows of dancers at New Year's, this is a matter of national ritual; though one's feelings may not be at ease, the rite cannot be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The six rows of dancers at New Year's are a matter of state ritual. One's feelings may be uneasy, but the ceremony cannot be set aside.

sentences.zh: 鐃吹軍樂，比之亦然，書疏方之，事則成小。

translations.literal: Cymbals, pipes, and military music are comparable in the same way; by contrast, letters and memorials are a smaller matter.
translations.idiomatic: Cymbals, pipes, and military music are comparable; letters and memorials, by contrast, are a smaller matter.

sentences.zh: 差可緣心。

translations.literal: This can somewhat follow the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Here one may more readily follow one's feelings.

sentences.zh: 聲樂自外，書疏自內，樂自他，書自己。

translations.literal: Music and song come from outside; letters and memorials come from within; music is from others, writing is from oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Music comes from outside, correspondence from within; music is imposed by others, writing is one's own.

sentences.zh: 劉僕之議，即情未安。

translations.literal: Secretary Liu's deliberation, as to feeling, is not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Liu's proposal does not sit right emotionally.

sentences.zh: 可令諸賢更共詳衷。」

translations.literal: Let the various worthies together examine this further in detail."
translations.idiomatic: Let the gentlemen reconsider this together in full."

sentences.zh: 司農卿明山賓、步兵校尉朱異議，稱「慕悼之解，宜終服月」。

translations.literal: Director of the Directorate of Agriculture Ming Shanbin and Commandant of Foot Soldiers Zhu Yi deliberated, stating, "The interpretation of mourning and lamentation should extend through the end of the mourning month."
translations.idiomatic: Director of Agriculture Ming Shanbin and Commandant of Foot Soldiers Zhu Yi ruled that the phrase mourning and lamentation should be used through the end of the mourning month.

sentences.zh: 於是付典書遵用，以為永准。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was handed to the Master of Documents to follow and use, establishing it as a permanent standard.
translations.idiomatic: The decision was then entrusted to the Master of Documents and adopted as permanent precedent.

sentences.zh: 七年十一月，貴嬪有疾，太子還永福省，朝夕侍疾，衣不解帶。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the seventh year, the noble consort fell ill; the crown prince returned to Yongfu Palace, attending her day and night without loosening his belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 7, when the noble consort fell ill, the crown prince returned to Yongfu Palace and nursed her day and night without undressing.

sentences.zh: 及薨，步從喪還宮，至殯，水漿不入口，每哭輒慟絕。

translations.literal: When she died, he walked behind the coffin back to the palace; until the encoffining, he took no food or drink, and each time he wept he would collapse in grief.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, he walked behind the coffin back to the palace. Until the encoffining he took neither food nor drink, and each time he wept he collapsed in grief.

sentences.zh: 武帝敕中書舍人顧協宣旨曰：「毀不滅性，聖人之制，不勝喪比於不孝。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu ordered Palace Secretary Gu Xie to convey the imperial message: "Ruining oneself without preserving one's nature is forbidden by the sages' rule; being unable to bear mourning is comparable to unfilial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sent Palace Secretary Gu Xie with this message: "The sages taught that one must not destroy one's health in mourning; failing to survive grief is itself a kind of unfilial conduct.

sentences.zh: 有我在，那得自毀如此。

translations.literal: While I am still here, how can you ruin yourself like this?
translations.idiomatic: I am still alive—how can you destroy yourself this way?

sentences.zh: 可即強進飲粥。」

translations.literal: You must at once force yourself to take gruel."
translations.idiomatic: Force yourself to take gruel at once."

sentences.zh: 太子奉敕，乃進數合，自是至葬，日進麥粥一升。

translations.literal: The crown prince obeyed the order and then took several mouthfuls; from then until the burial, he took one sheng of barley gruel each day.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince obeyed and took a few mouthfuls. From then until the burial he consumed one sheng of barley gruel each day.

sentences.zh: 武帝又敕曰：「聞汝所進過少，轉就羸瘦。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu again ordered, "I hear that what you take is too little and you are growing increasingly emaciated.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu wrote again, "I hear you are eating too little and growing thinner by the day.

sentences.zh: 我比更無餘病，政為汝如此，胸中亦填塞成疾。

translations.literal: I myself have no other illness; it is precisely because of you like this that my chest also fills and becomes diseased.
translations.idiomatic: I have no other illness myself—it is worry for you that fills my chest and makes me ill.

sentences.zh: 故應強加饘粥，不俟我恒爾懸心。」

translations.literal: Therefore you should force yourself to take more gruel, and not wait until I am constantly anxious in this way."
translations.idiomatic: Eat more gruel by force, and spare me this constant anxiety."

sentences.zh: 雖屢奉敕勸逼，終喪日止一溢，不嚐菜果之味。

translations.literal: Though repeatedly urged by imperial order, throughout the mourning period he took only one yi per day and never tasted vegetables or fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Though repeatedly pressed by imperial command, throughout the mourning period he ate only one yi a day and never tasted vegetables or fruit.

sentences.zh: 體素壯，腰帶十圍，至是減削過半。

translations.literal: His body had been naturally robust, his waist belt ten wei in girth; by this time it had been reduced by more than half.
translations.idiomatic: He had been naturally robust, with a waist ten wei around; by now it had shrunk by more than half.

sentences.zh: 每入朝，士庶見者莫不下泣。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered court, none among officials and commoners who saw him failed to weep.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he appeared at court, officials and commoners alike wept at the sight of him.

sentences.zh: 太子自加元服，帝便使省萬機，內外百司奏事者填塞於前。

translations.literal: From the time the crown prince received his capping ceremony, the emperor had him oversee the myriad affairs of state; memorials from the hundred offices within and without piled up before him.
translations.idiomatic: After his coming-of-age ceremony, the emperor put him in charge of state affairs, and memorials from every office piled up before him.

sentences.zh: 太子明于庶事，每所奏謬誤巧妄，皆即辯析，示其可否，徐令改正，未嘗彈糾一人。

translations.literal: The crown prince was clear about ordinary affairs; whenever memorials contained errors, deceptions, or fabrications, he immediately analyzed them, showing what was acceptable and what was not, and slowly had them corrected, never once punishing a person.
translations.idiomatic: He had a clear grasp of routine business. Whenever a memorial contained errors or fabrications, he analyzed it on the spot, explained what was acceptable and what was not, and had it corrected without ever punishing anyone.

sentences.zh: 平斷法獄，多所全宥，天下皆稱仁。

translations.literal: In judging legal cases he showed leniency and spared many; all under heaven praised his benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: In legal judgments he showed mercy and spared many lives, and the realm praised his benevolence.

sentences.zh: 性寬和容眾，喜慍不形於色。

translations.literal: By nature he was generous and tolerant of others; pleasure and anger never showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Generous and tolerant by nature, he never let pleasure or anger show on his face.

sentences.zh: 引納才學之士，賞愛無倦。

translations.literal: He drew in men of talent and learning and never tired of honoring and cherishing them.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed men of talent and learning and never tired of encouraging them.

sentences.zh: 恒自討論墳籍，或與學士商榷古今，繼以文章著述，率以為常。

translations.literal: He constantly discussed himself the classics, or debated past and present with scholars, followed by literary composition—this became his daily habit.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly studied the classics on his own, debated history with scholars, and wrote—this was his daily routine.

sentences.zh: 于時東宮有書幾三萬卷，名才並集，文學之盛，晉、宋以來未之有也。

translations.literal: At that time the Eastern Palace had nearly thirty thousand volumes of books; eminent talents all gathered there, and the flourishing of letters had not been seen since Jin and Song.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace held nearly thirty thousand volumes, and eminent talents gathered there in numbers unmatched since the Jin and Song dynasties.

sentences.zh: 性愛山水，于玄圃穿築，更立亭館，與朝士名素者遊其中。

translations.literal: By nature he loved mountains and waters; in the Mystic Garden he dug and built, establishing pavilions and halls anew, and wandered there with renowned court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He loved landscape and scenery. In the Mystic Garden he excavated ponds and built new pavilions, where he wandered with distinguished court gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 嘗泛舟後池，番禺侯軌盛稱此中宜奏女樂。

translations.literal: Once, while boating on the rear pond, Marquis of Panyu Gui lavishly praised how suitable this place was for female musicians to perform.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while boating on the rear pond, Marquis of Panyu Gui enthusiastically suggested that female musicians should perform there.

sentences.zh: 太子不答，詠左思招隱詩云：「何必絲與竹，山水有清音。」

translations.literal: The crown prince did not reply but recited from Zuo Si's Poem Summoning the Recluse: "Why need silk and bamboo? Mountains and waters have pure sounds."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince made no reply but recited from Zuo Si's Poem Summoning the Recluse: "Why need strings and pipes? The mountains and waters have their own pure music."

sentences.zh: 軌慚而止。

translations.literal: Gui, ashamed, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, abashed, said no more.

sentences.zh: 出宮二十餘年，不畜音聲。

translations.literal: For more than twenty years after leaving the inner palace, he kept no music.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years after leaving the inner palace, he kept no musicians.

sentences.zh: 未薨少時，敕賜太樂女伎一部，略非所好。

translations.literal: Shortly before his death, an edict bestowed upon him a troupe of female performers from the Imperial Music Office, which was hardly to his taste.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly before his death, the emperor granted him a troupe of female performers from the Imperial Music Office, which held little appeal for him.

sentences.zh: 普通中，大軍北侵，都下米貴。

translations.literal: During the Putong era, the great army invaded from the north, and rice in the capital grew dear.
translations.idiomatic: During the Putong era, when northern armies invaded, rice in the capital became scarce and costly.

sentences.zh: 太子因命菲衣減膳。

translations.literal: The crown prince therefore ordered plain dress and reduced meals.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince responded by adopting plain dress and cutting back his meals.

sentences.zh: 每霖雨積雪，遣腹心左右周行閭巷，視貧困家及有流離道路，以米密加振賜，人十石。

translations.literal: Whenever there was long rain or accumulated snow, he sent trusted attendants to patrol lanes and alleys, observing impoverished households and those wandering destitute on the roads, and secretly added relief grants of ten shi of rice per person.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever heavy rain or snow fell, he sent trusted attendants through the lanes to find poor households and people stranded on the roads, quietly giving each person ten shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 又出主衣絹帛，年常多作襦褲，各三千領，冬月以施寒者，不令人知。

translations.literal: He also supplied silk from the palace stores, each year having many jackets and trousers made—three thousand of each—and in winter months distributing them to those suffering from cold, without letting people know.
translations.idiomatic: He also drew on palace stores of silk to have three thousand jackets and three thousand pairs of trousers made each year, distributing them in winter to those in need without publicity.

sentences.zh: 若死亡無可斂，則為備棺槥。

translations.literal: If someone died with no means for burial, he provided coffins.
translations.idiomatic: When the dead had no means of burial, he provided coffins.

sentences.zh: 每聞遠近百姓賦役勤苦，輒斂容變色。

translations.literal: Whenever he heard that common people near and far suffered from heavy taxes and corvée labor, he immediately composed his expression and changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he heard that people near and far were burdened by taxes and corvée labor, his face would darken with concern.

sentences.zh: 常以戶口未實，重于勞擾。

translations.literal: He constantly regarded the failure to register households accurately as more serious than the burden of labor and disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: He regarded inaccurate household registration as a graver problem than the burden of labor itself.

sentences.zh: 吳興郡屢以水災不熟，有上言當漕大瀆以瀉浙江。

translations.literal: Wuxing Commandery repeatedly failed to ripen crops due to flood disasters; someone submitted a memorial proposing that the Great Canal be dredged to drain into the Qiantang River.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxing Commandery repeatedly lost its harvest to floods, and a memorial proposed dredging the Great Canal to drain floodwaters into the Qiantang River.

sentences.zh: 中大通二年春，詔遣前交州刺史王弈假節發吳、吳興、信義三郡人丁就役。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Zhongdatong, an edict dispatched former Governor of Jiaozhou Wang Yi with provisional credentials to mobilize corvée laborers from the three commanderies of Wu, Wuxing, and Xinyi for service.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Zhongdatong 2, an edict sent former Governor of Jiaozhou Wang Yi with provisional authority to conscript labor from Wu, Wuxing, and Xinyi commanderies.

sentences.zh: 太子上疏曰：「伏聞當遣王弈等上東三郡人丁開漕溝渠，導泄震澤，使吳興一境無復水災，暫勞永逸，必獲後利。

translations.literal: The crown prince submitted a memorial, saying, "I have heard that Wang Yi and others are to be sent to mobilize corvée labor from the three eastern commanderies to open canals and ditches, channeling and draining Lake Zhen, so that the whole region of Wuxing will no longer suffer flood disasters—a brief labor for lasting ease, surely yielding future benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince submitted a memorial: "I understand that Wang Yi and others are to conscript labor from the three eastern commanderies to dredge canals and drain Lake Zhen, ending floods in Wuxing—a short-term burden for long-term gain.

sentences.zh: 未萌難睹，竊有愚懷。

translations.literal: What has not yet sprouted is hard to see; I privately harbor humble thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: The future is hard to foresee, and I have some modest concerns.

sentences.zh: 所聞吳興累年失收，人頗流移，吳郡十城，亦不全熟，唯信義去秋有稔，復非恒役之民。

translations.literal: What I have heard is that Wuxing for successive years has failed to harvest, and many people have drifted away; of the ten cities of Wu Commandery, not all have fully ripened crops, and only Xinyi had a good harvest last autumn—yet these are not people accustomed to regular corvée.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that Wuxing has lost harvests for years and many people have fled. In Wu Commandery's ten cities, not all crops have ripened; only Xinyi had a good harvest last autumn, and even there the people are not used to regular corvée.

sentences.zh: 即日東境穀稼猶貴，劫盜屢起，在所有司，皆不聞奏。

translations.literal: At present grain in the eastern region is still dear, and banditry repeatedly arises; the officials in charge all fail to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Even now grain in the east remains costly and banditry is frequent, yet local officials report none of it.

sentences.zh: 今征戍未歸，強丁疏少，此雖小舉，竊恐難合。

translations.literal: Now those conscripted for garrison duty have not returned, and able-bodied men are few and scattered; though this is a small undertaking, I privately fear it will be hard to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Conscripts have not yet returned from garrison duty, and able-bodied men are scarce. Though this seems a small project, I fear it will be hard to carry out.

sentences.zh: 吏一呼門，動為人蠹。

translations.literal: When an official calls at the door, he invariably becomes a plague upon the people.
translations.idiomatic: When officials come knocking, they invariably become a plague on the people.

sentences.zh: 又出丁之處，遠近不一，比得齊集，已妨蠶農。

translations.literal: Moreover, the places from which laborers are drawn are at varying distances; by the time they can be assembled, silkworm season and farming are already disrupted.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers must come from places near and far, and by the time they assemble, silkworm season and farming will already be disrupted.

sentences.zh: 去年稱為豐歲，公私未能足食，如復今茲失業，慮恐為弊更深。

translations.literal: Last year was called a bountiful year, yet public and private stores still could not fully feed the people; if this year again loses productive work, I fear the harm will be even deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Last year was called a good harvest, yet public and private stores still fell short. If people lose work again this year, the harm may run even deeper.

sentences.zh: 且草竊多伺候人間虛實，若善人從役，則抄盜彌增。

translations.literal: Moreover, petty bandits often watch for the true state of affairs among the people; if good people are sent to corvée, plunder and theft will only increase.
translations.idiomatic: Petty bandits watch for weakness among the people. If good citizens are sent to corvée, robbery will only increase.

sentences.zh: 吳興未受其益，內地已離其弊。

translations.literal: Wuxing has not yet received the benefit, while the interior has already suffered the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxing has not yet gained the benefit, while the interior has already borne the cost.

sentences.zh: 不審可得權停此功，待優實以不？」

translations.literal: I do not know whether this project may be temporarily halted, to wait until conditions are more favorable—is this possible?"
translations.idiomatic: Might this project be suspended for now until conditions improve?"

sentences.zh: 武帝優詔以喻焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu issued a gracious edict to explain the matter to him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu replied with a gracious edict explaining his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 太子孝謹天至，每入朝，未五鼓便守城門開。

translations.literal: The crown prince's filial reverence reached heaven itself; whenever he attended court, before the fifth watch he would already be waiting at the city gate for it to open.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's filial devotion was extraordinary. Whenever he attended court, he waited at the city gate before the fifth watch for it to open.

sentences.zh: 東宮雖燕居內殿，一坐一起，恒向西南面台。

translations.literal: Though the Eastern Palace was at ease dwelling in the inner halls, whenever he sat or rose he always faced southwest toward the imperial terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Even at rest in the Eastern Palace, whenever he sat or stood he always faced southwest toward the imperial terrace.

sentences.zh: 宿被召當入，危坐達旦。

translations.literal: If summoned the night before to enter court, he would sit upright until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: If summoned the night before, he would sit upright until dawn.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，游後池，乘雕文舸摘芙蓉。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year, he toured the rear pond, riding a carved-pattern boat to pick lotus flowers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 3, he toured the rear pond in an ornately carved boat, picking lotus flowers.

sentences.zh: 姬人蕩舟，沒溺而得出，因動股，恐貽帝憂，深誡不言，以寢疾聞。

translations.literal: A concubine rocked the boat; he sank and nearly drowned before getting out, injuring his thigh in the process. Fearing it would cause the emperor worry, he strictly forbade anyone to speak of it and had it reported as a lingering illness.
translations.idiomatic: A concubine rocked the boat; he nearly drowned before climbing out, injuring his thigh. Fearing it would worry the emperor, he forbade anyone to speak of it and had the matter reported as a lingering illness.

sentences.zh: 武帝敕看問，輒自力手書啟。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ordered inquiries about his condition, he always forced himself to write memorials in his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu sent inquiries, he always forced himself to write replies in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 及稍篤，左右欲啟聞，猶不許，曰：「雲何令至尊知我如此惡。」

translations.literal: When his condition grew somewhat grave, those around him wished to report it, but he still would not allow it, saying, "Why should I let His Majesty know I am this ill?"
translations.idiomatic: When his condition worsened, his attendants wanted to inform the emperor, but he still refused, saying, "Why should I let His Majesty know how ill I am?"

sentences.zh: 因便嗚咽。

translations.literal: And thereupon he sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: And he broke into sobs.

sentences.zh: 四月乙巳，暴惡，馳啟武帝，比至已薨，時年三十一。

translations.literal: On the yisi day of the fourth month, he suddenly took a turn for the worse; an urgent memorial was sent to Emperor Wu, but by the time he arrived, the crown prince had already died, aged thirty-one.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of the fourth month he suddenly worsened. An urgent message was sent to Emperor Wu, but by the time he arrived the crown prince was dead, aged thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 帝臨哭盡哀，詔斂以袞冕，諡曰昭明。

translations.literal: The emperor came to weep with full grief and ordered him enshrouded in imperial robes and cap, posthumously naming him Zhaoming.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to mourn with full grief, ordered him enshrouded in imperial robes, and gave him the posthumous name Zhaoming.

sentences.zh: 五月庚寅，葬安寧陵，詔司徒左長史王筠為哀冊文。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day of the fifth month, he was buried at Anning Mausoleum; an edict appointed Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education Wang Yun to compose the elegiac encomium.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day of the fifth month he was buried at Anning Mausoleum. An edict commissioned Left Chief Administrator Wang Yun of the Ministry of Education to compose the elegiac encomium.

sentences.zh: 朝野惋愕，都下男女奔走宮門，號泣滿路。

translations.literal: Court and countryside were struck with grief and shock; men and women of the capital rushed to the palace gates, wailing until the roads were filled with cries.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside were stunned with grief. Men and women of the capital rushed to the palace gates, filling the roads with wailing.

sentences.zh: 四方甿庶及疆徼之人，聞喪皆哀慟。

translations.literal: Common people from the four directions and those on the frontier borders, upon hearing of the death, all mourned in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners throughout the realm and people on the frontiers all mourned upon hearing the news.

sentences.zh: 太子性仁恕，見在宮禁防捉荊子者，問之，雲以清道驅人。

translations.literal: The crown prince was benevolent and forgiving by nature. Seeing those in the palace precincts armed with thorn whips to seize people, he asked about it and was told they were clearing the road by driving people away.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was naturally benevolent and forgiving. Seeing palace guards with thorn whips seizing people, he asked why and was told they were clearing the road.

sentences.zh: 太子恐復致痛，使捉手板代之。

translations.literal: The crown prince feared they would again cause pain and had them hold writing tablets instead.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing they would hurt people again, he had them carry writing tablets instead.

sentences.zh: 頻食中得蠅蟲之屬，密置柈邊，恐廚人獲罪，不令人知。

translations.literal: He frequently found flies, insects, and the like in his food and secretly placed them at the edge of the plate, fearing the kitchen staff would be punished, and never let anyone know.
translations.idiomatic: When he found flies or insects in his food, he quietly set them aside, fearing the kitchen staff would be punished, and never told anyone.

sentences.zh: 又見後合小兒攤戲，後屬有獄牒攤者法，士人結流徒，庶人結徒。

translations.literal: He also saw young boys in the rear quarters gambling, and later there was a legal statute on gambling: scholars were sentenced to exile with penal servitude, commoners to penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: He also saw young boys in the rear quarters gambling. Later a law on gambling sentenced scholars to exile with penal servitude and commoners to penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「私錢自戲，不犯公物，此科太重。」

translations.literal: The crown prince said, "Gambling with one's own private money for amusement, without violating public property—this statute is too severe."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "Gambling with one's own money for amusement, without touching public property—this penalty is too harsh."

sentences.zh: 令注刑止三歲，士人免官。

translations.literal: He ordered that the penalty be limited to three years, and scholars merely dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the penalty reduced to three years, with scholars merely dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 獄牒應死者必降長徒，自此以下莫不減半。

translations.literal: In legal cases where death was warranted, the sentence was invariably reduced to long-term penal servitude; from this level downward, none were not halved.
translations.idiomatic: Cases warranting death were invariably commuted to long-term penal servitude, and lesser sentences were all halved.

sentences.zh: 所著文集二十卷，又撰古今典誥文言為正序十卷，五言詩之善者為英華集二十卷，文選三十卷。

translations.literal: His collected writings numbered twenty volumes; he also compiled Correct Prefaces in ten volumes, selecting classical edicts and proclamations in literary language from past and present; Selected Excellence in twenty volumes, gathering fine five-character poems; and Literary Anthology in thirty volumes.
translations.idiomatic: He authored a twenty-volume collected works, plus Correct Prefaces in ten volumes of classical edicts and proclamations, Selected Excellence in twenty volumes of fine five-character poetry, and the thirty-volume Literary Anthology.

sentences.zh: 初，丁貴嬪薨，太子遣人求得善墓地，將斬草，有賣地者因閹人俞三副求巿，若得三百萬，許以百萬與之。

translations.literal: Initially, when Noble Consort Ding died, the crown prince sent men to find a good burial site. As they were about to cut the grass, a land seller, through the eunuch Yu Sanfu, sought to sell it; if he could obtain three million, he promised to give one million to Sanfu.
translations.idiomatic: When Noble Consort Ding died, the crown prince sent men to find a good burial site. As they were clearing the ground, a landowner, through the eunuch Yu Sanfu, offered to sell the plot for three million, promising Sanfu one million.

sentences.zh: 三副密啟武帝，言太子所得地不如今所得地于帝吉，帝末年多忌，便命巿之。

translations.literal: Sanfu secretly reported to Emperor Wu that the land the crown prince had obtained was not as auspicious for the emperor as the land now offered; in his later years the emperor was much given to suspicion, and he ordered it purchased.
translations.idiomatic: Sanfu secretly told Emperor Wu that the crown prince's chosen site was less auspicious for the emperor than this new one. In his later years the emperor was deeply suspicious, and he ordered the land purchased.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，有道士善圖墓，云：「地不利長子，若厭伏或可申延。」

translations.literal: After the burial was complete, a Daoist skilled in geomancy of tombs said, "This site is unfavorable to the eldest son; if suppressive rites are performed, his life may perhaps be extended."
translations.idiomatic: After the burial, a Daoist skilled in tomb geomancy said, "This site is harmful to the eldest son. Suppressive rites might prolong his life."

sentences.zh: 乃為蠟鵝及諸物埋墓側長子位。

translations.literal: Thereupon wax geese and various objects were made and buried beside the tomb at the position of the eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Wax geese and other objects were then buried beside the tomb at the eldest son's position.

sentences.zh: 有宮監鮑邈之、魏雅者，二人初並為太子所愛，邈之晚見疏於雅，密啟武帝云：「雅為太子厭禱。」

translations.literal: There were palace supervisors Bao Miaozhi and Wei Ya; both were initially favored by the crown prince, but Miaozhi later came to be estranged in favor of Ya. He secretly reported to Emperor Wu, saying, "Ya performed suppressive prayers for the crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: Palace supervisors Bao Miaozhi and Wei Ya were both once favored by the crown prince, but Miaozhi later fell out of favor to Ya. He secretly told Emperor Wu, "Ya performed curse-suppression rites for the crown prince."

sentences.zh: 帝密遣檢掘，果得鵝等物。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly sent men to investigate and dig, and indeed found geese and other objects.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly sent men to dig, and they found the geese and other objects.

sentences.zh: 大驚，將窮其事。

translations.literal: Greatly alarmed, he was about to pursue the matter to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Greatly alarmed, he was about to investigate the matter fully.

sentences.zh: 徐勉固諫得止，於是唯誅道士，由是太子迄終以此慚慨，故其嗣不立。

translations.literal: Xu Mian firmly remonstrated and stopped it; thereupon only the Daoist was executed. From this the crown prince until his death bore shame and resentment over the matter, and therefore his heir was not established.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mian's firm remonstrance stopped the investigation; only the Daoist was executed. The crown prince carried shame and resentment over this until his death, and his heir was never established.

sentences.zh: 後邵陵王臨丹陽郡，因邈之與鄉人爭婢，議以為誘略之罪牒宮，簡文追感太子冤，揮淚誅之。

translations.literal: Later, when Prince of Shaoling governed Danyang Commandery, because Miaozhi disputed a maidservant with a fellow townsman, the case was judged as the crime of enticement and abduction and reported to the palace. Emperor Jianwen, recalling the crown prince's wrong, wept as he ordered Miaozhi executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Prince of Shaoling governed Danyang, Miaozhi disputed a maidservant with a fellow townsman. The case was judged enticement and reported to court. Emperor Jianwen, recalling the crown prince's injustice, wept as he ordered Miaozhi executed.

sentences.zh: 邈之兄子僧隆為宮直，前未知邈之侄，即日驅出。

translations.literal: Miaozhi's elder brother's son Senglong served as a palace attendant; not having known he was Miaozhi's nephew, he was driven out that same day.
translations.idiomatic: Miaozhi's nephew Senglong, a palace attendant who had not known of the connection, was expelled the same day.

sentences.zh: 棟字元吉。

translations.literal: Dong, styled Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Dong, styled Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 及簡文見廢，侯景奉以為主。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen was deposed, Hou Jing installed him as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jianwen was deposed, Hou Jing installed him as emperor.

sentences.zh: 棟方與妃張氏鋤葵，而法駕奄至，棟驚不知所為，泣而升輦。

translations.literal: Dong was just hoeing sunflowers with his consort Lady Zhang when the imperial carriage suddenly arrived. Dong, startled and not knowing what to do, wept as he mounted the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Dong was hoeing sunflowers with his consort Lady Zhang when the imperial carriage suddenly arrived. Startled and at a loss, he wept as he mounted the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 及即位，升武德殿，欻有回風從地湧起，翻飛華蓋，徑出端門，時人知其不終。

translations.literal: When he took the throne and ascended Wude Hall, suddenly a whirlwind surged up from the ground, overturning and blowing away the imperial canopy straight out through Duan Gate; people of the time knew he would not reach the end.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne and ascended Wude Hall, a whirlwind suddenly surged from the ground, overturning the imperial canopy and blowing it out through Duan Gate. People knew his reign would not last.

sentences.zh: 於是年號天正，追尊昭明太子曰昭明皇帝，安王為安皇帝，金華敬妃蔡氏為敬皇后，太妃王氏為皇太后，妃為皇后。

translations.literal: Thereupon the era name was Tianzheng; Crown Prince Zhaoming was posthumously honored as Emperor Zhaoming, Prince An as Emperor An, Respectful Consort Cai of Jinhua as Empress Jing, Grand Consort Wang as Empress Dowager, and his consort as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: He adopted the era name Tianzheng and posthumously honored Crown Prince Zhaoming as Emperor Zhaoming, Prince An as Emperor An, Respectful Consort Cai of Jinhua as Empress Jing, Grand Consort Wang as Empress Dowager, and his own consort as Empress.

sentences.zh: 未幾，行禪讓禮，棟封淮陰王，及二弟橋、樛，並鎖於密室。

translations.literal: Before long the abdication rites were performed; Dong was enfeoffed as Prince of Huaiyin, and his two younger brothers Qiao and Jiao were both locked in a sealed chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he performed the abdication rites. Dong was enfeoffed as Prince of Huaiyin, and his two younger brothers Qiao and Jiao were locked in a sealed chamber.

sentences.zh: 景敗走，兄弟相扶出，逢杜崱於道，崱去其鎖。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing fled in defeat, the brothers supported each other out and met Du Kan on the road; Kan removed their shackles.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing fled in defeat, the brothers helped each other out and met Du Kan on the road, who removed their shackles.

sentences.zh: 弟曰：「今日免橫死矣。」

translations.literal: The younger brother said, "Today we have escaped violent death."
translations.idiomatic: The younger brother said, "Today we have escaped violent death."

sentences.zh: 棟曰：「倚伏難知，吾猶有懼。」

translations.literal: Dong said, "Fortune and misfortune are hard to know; I still have fear."
translations.idiomatic: Dong said, "Fortune and misfortune are unpredictable. I am still afraid."

sentences.zh: 初，王僧辯之為都督，將發，諮元帝曰：「平賊之後，嗣君萬福，未審有何儀注？」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Sengbian was commander-in-chief and about to set out, he consulted Emperor Yuan, saying, "After the rebels are pacified, may the heir enjoy boundless fortune—I do not know what ceremonies are prescribed?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Wang Sengbian was about to set out as commander-in-chief, he asked Emperor Yuan, "After the rebels are defeated, what ceremonies should be observed for the heir?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「六門之內，自極兵威。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Within the six gates, apply military force to the utmost."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Within the six gates, use military force to the fullest."

sentences.zh: 僧辯曰：「平賊之謀，臣為己任，成濟之事，請別舉人。」

translations.literal: Sengbian said, "The plan to pacify the rebels is my own responsibility; the matter of Cheng Ji, please appoint someone else."
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian said, "Defeating the rebels is my responsibility. For the matter of Cheng Ji, please appoint someone else."

sentences.zh: 由是帝別敕宣猛將軍朱買臣使行忍酷。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor separately ordered General of Manifest Valor Zhu Maichen to carry out ruthless cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then separately ordered General of Manifest Valor Zhu Maichen to carry out the ruthless deed.

sentences.zh: 會簡文已被害，棟等與買臣遇見，呼往船共飲，未竟，並沈于水。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Jianwen had already been killed; Dong and the others encountered Maichen, who called them to his boat to drink together, and before they finished, all were drowned in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen had already been killed. Dong and the others met Maichen, who invited them to his boat to drink. Before they finished, all were drowned.

sentences.zh: 河東王譽字重孫，普通二年，封枝江縣公。

translations.literal: Prince of Hedong Yu, styled Chongsun; in the second year of Putong he was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhijiang County.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hedong Yu, styled Chongsun, was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhijiang County in Putong 2.

sentences.zh: 中大通三年，改封河東郡王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong, he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Hedong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong 3 he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 累遷南中郎將、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to General of the Southern Palace Guard and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of the Southern Palace Guard and Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，侯景寇建鄴，譽入援，至青草湖，台城沒，有詔班師。

translations.literal: Before long Hou Jing invaded Jiankang; Yu marched to the rescue, reaching Qingcao Lake, but the capital fell and an edict ordered withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hou Jing attacked Jiankang. Yu marched to the rescue and reached Qingcao Lake, but the capital fell and an edict ordered withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 譽還湘鎮。

translations.literal: Yu returned to his post in Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu returned to his post in Xiang.

sentences.zh: 時元帝軍于武城，新除雍州刺史張纘密報元帝曰：「河東起兵，岳陽聚米，將來襲江陵。」

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Yuan was encamped at Wucheng; the newly appointed Governor of Yongzhou Zhang Zan secretly reported to Emperor Yuan, saying, "Prince of Hedong has raised troops; Yueyang is gathering grain—he will soon come to attack Jiangling."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was encamped at Wucheng when the newly appointed Governor of Yongzhou Zhang Zan secretly reported, "Prince of Hedong has raised troops and Yueyang is stockpiling grain. He will soon attack Jiangling."

sentences.zh: 元帝甚懼，沈米斷纜而歸。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan was greatly afraid; he sank the grain and cut the mooring ropes to return.
translations.idiomatic: Greatly alarmed, Emperor Yuan sank his grain stores, cut his mooring ropes, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 因遣諮議周弘直至譽所督其糧眾。

translations.literal: He then dispatched Adviser Zhou Hongzhi to Yu's headquarters to oversee his grain and troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Adviser Zhou Hongzhi to Yu's headquarters to take charge of his grain and troops.

sentences.zh: 譽曰：「各自軍府，何忽隸人。」

translations.literal: Yu said, "Each has his own military headquarters—why suddenly make me subordinate to another?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Each of us has his own command—why should I suddenly become someone else's subordinate?"

sentences.zh: 使三反，譽並不從。

translations.literal: The messenger was sent three times, but Yu would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The order was sent three times, but Yu refused each time.

sentences.zh: 元帝大怒，遣世子方等征之，反為譽敗死。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan was greatly angered and dispatched his heir Fangdeng to campaign against him, but Fangdeng was instead defeated and killed by Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was furious and sent his heir Fangdeng against him, but Fangdeng was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 又令信州刺史鮑泉討譽，並陳示禍福。

translations.literal: He then ordered Governor of Xinzhou Bao Quan to attack Yu, also setting forth the consequences of fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Governor of Xinzhou Bao Quan to attack Yu, also explaining the consequences.

sentences.zh: 譽謂曰：「欲前即前，無所多說。」

translations.literal: Yu said to him, "If you wish to advance, then advance—there is nothing more to say."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "If you want to advance, then advance. There is nothing more to say."

sentences.zh: 泉軍于石槨寺，譽逆擊不利而還。

translations.literal: Quan's army encamped at Shiguang Temple; Yu counterattacked but was unsuccessful and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Quan encamped at Shiguang Temple. Yu counterattacked but failed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 泉進軍橘洲，譽攻之又見敗。

translations.literal: Quan advanced to Juzhou; Yu attacked again and was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Quan advanced to Juzhou. Yu attacked again and was defeated once more.

sentences.zh: 於是遂圍之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: Quan then besieged him.

sentences.zh: 譽幼而驍勇，馬上用弩，兼有膽氣，能撫士卒，甚得眾心。

translations.literal: Yu from youth was fierce and brave, skilled with crossbow on horseback, and possessed both courage and daring; he could comfort soldiers and won their hearts deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had been fierce and brave from youth, skilled with a crossbow on horseback. Courageous and able to win over his troops, he enjoyed deep loyalty.

sentences.zh: 元帝又遣領軍王僧辯代鮑泉攻譽。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan again dispatched Commander-in-Chief Wang Sengbian to replace Bao Quan in attacking Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan then sent Commander-in-Chief Wang Sengbian to replace Bao Quan and attack Yu.

sentences.zh: 譽將潰圍而出，會其麾下將慕容華引僧辯入城，遂被執。

translations.literal: Yu was about to break out of the encirclement when his subordinate general Murong Hua led Sengbian into the city, and he was thereupon captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was about to break out when his subordinate Murong Hua let Sengbian into the city, and Yu was captured.

sentences.zh: 謂守者曰：「勿殺我，得一見七官，申此讒賊，死無恨。」

translations.literal: He said to his guards, "Do not kill me; let me see the Seventh Officer once to explain this slanderous villain, and I will die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: He told his guards, "Do not kill me. Let me see the Seventh Officer once to expose this slanderer, and I will die without regret."

sentences.zh: 主者曰：「奉令不許。」

translations.literal: The officer in charge said, "By order this is not permitted."
translations.idiomatic: The officer in charge said, "Orders forbid it."

sentences.zh: 遂斬首，送荊鎮。

translations.literal: Thereupon his head was cut off and sent to the Jing garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His head was cut off and sent to the Jing garrison.

sentences.zh: 元帝返其首以葬焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan returned his head for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan returned his head for burial.

sentences.zh: 初，譽之將敗，引鏡照面，不見其頭。

translations.literal: Earlier, as Yu was about to be defeated, he held up a mirror to his face and could not see his head.
translations.idiomatic: Before his defeat, Yu held a mirror to his face and could not see his head.

sentences.zh: 又見長人蓋屋，兩手據地噉其臍。

translations.literal: He also saw a tall man covering the house, both hands on the ground biting at his navel.
translations.idiomatic: He also dreamed of a giant covering the house, hands on the ground, biting at his navel.

sentences.zh: 又見白狗大如驢，從城出，不知所在。

translations.literal: He also saw a white dog as large as a donkey leaving the city, not knowing where it went.
translations.idiomatic: He also saw a white dog as large as a donkey leave the city and vanish.

sentences.zh: 譽甚惡之，俄而城陷。

translations.literal: Yu regarded these as very ill omens, and soon the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Yu took these as terrible omens, and soon the city fell.

sentences.zh: 豫章王綜字世謙，武帝第二子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang Zong, styled Shiqian, was Emperor Wu's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yuzhang Zong, styled Shiqian, was Emperor Wu's second son.

sentences.zh: 天監三年，封豫章郡王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjian he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 3 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 累遷北中郎將、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to General of the Northern Palace Guard and Governor of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of the Northern Palace Guard and Governor of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中、鎮右將軍。

translations.literal: He entered court as Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the Right.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the Right.

sentences.zh: 初，綜母吳淑媛在齊東昏宮，寵在潘、餘之亞。

translations.literal: Initially, Zong's mother Lady Wu had been in the palace of Qi Emperor Donghun, her favor ranking below Pan and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's mother Lady Wu had served in the palace of Qi Emperor Donghun, where her favor ranked below Pan and Yu.

sentences.zh: 及得幸于武帝，七月而生綜，宮中多疑之。

translations.literal: When she gained favor with Emperor Wu and gave birth to Zong in the seventh month, many in the palace were suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When she won Emperor Wu's favor and gave birth to Zong in the seventh month, many in the palace were suspicious.

sentences.zh: 淑媛寵衰怨望。

translations.literal: As Lady Wu's favor waned, she harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: As Lady Wu's favor waned, she grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 及綜年十四五，恒夢一年少肥壯自挈其首對綜，如此非一，綜轉成長，心驚不已。

translations.literal: When Zong was fourteen or fifteen, he constantly dreamed of a young, stout man holding up his own severed head before Zong; this happened more than once. As Zong grew older, his heart was ceaselessly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong was fourteen or fifteen, he repeatedly dreamed of a stout young man holding up his own severed head before him. As he grew older, he was constantly unsettled.

sentences.zh: 頻密問淑媛曰：「夢何所如？」

translations.literal: He frequently and closely asked Lady Wu, "What are the dreams like?"
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly pressed Lady Wu, "What do the dreams look like?"

sentences.zh: 夢既不一，淑媛問夢中形色，頗類東昏。

translations.literal: The dreams were not all the same; Lady Wu asked about the figure's appearance in the dreams, which closely resembled Donghun.
translations.idiomatic: The dreams varied, but when Lady Wu asked about the figure's appearance, it closely resembled Donghun.

sentences.zh: 因密報之曰：「汝七月日生兒，安得比諸皇子。

translations.literal: She therefore secretly informed him, saying, "You were born in the seventh month—how can you compare with the other princes?
translations.idiomatic: She secretly told him, "You were born in the seventh month. How can you compare with the other princes?

sentences.zh: 汝今太子次弟，幸保富貴勿泄。」

translations.literal: You are now the crown prince's next younger brother; fortunately preserve your wealth and status and do not reveal this."
translations.idiomatic: You are the crown prince's next younger brother. Keep your fortune and tell no one."

sentences.zh: 綜相抱哭，每日夜恒泫泣。

translations.literal: They embraced each other and wept; day and night Zong constantly shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: They embraced and wept. Day and night Zong wept without cease.

sentences.zh: 又每靜室閉戶，藉地被髮席藳。

translations.literal: He also often shut himself in a quiet room, spreading straw mats on the ground, letting down his hair, and sleeping on straw.
translations.idiomatic: He also shut himself in quiet rooms, let down his hair, and slept on straw mats on the floor.

sentences.zh: 輕財好士，分施不輟，唯留身上故衣，外齋接客，分粗服。

translations.literal: He was generous with wealth and fond of scholars, distributing gifts without cease, keeping only his worn clothes on his body; in the outer study when receiving guests, he wore coarse garments.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous with wealth and fond of scholars, giving constantly and keeping only his worn clothes. When receiving guests in his outer study, he wore coarse garments.

sentences.zh: 廚庫恒致罄乏。

translations.literal: The kitchen stores constantly reached exhaustion and shortage.
translations.idiomatic: The kitchen stores were constantly empty.

sentences.zh: 常于內齋布沙於地，終日跣行，足下生胝，日能行三百里。

translations.literal: He often spread sand on the floor of the inner study and walked barefoot all day; calluses formed on the soles of his feet, and he could walk three hundred li in a day.
translations.idiomatic: He often spread sand on the floor of his inner study and walked barefoot all day until calluses formed on his soles. He could walk three hundred li in a day.

sentences.zh: 嘗有人士姓王，以屯躓投告綜。

translations.literal: Once a gentleman surnamed Wang, having suffered hardship and setback, came to Zong to plead for help.
translations.idiomatic: Once a gentleman named Wang, fallen on hard times, came to Zong for help.

sentences.zh: 于時大乏，唯有眠床故皁復帳，即下付之。

translations.literal: At the time supplies were greatly lacking; he had only an old dark cloth coverlet from his sleeping couch, which he immediately took down and gave to him.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies were scarce; he had only an old dark cloth coverlet from his bed, which he immediately gave away.

sentences.zh: 其降意下士，以伺風雲之會，諸侯王妃主及外人並知此懷，唯武帝不疑。

translations.literal: He lowered himself to win over scholars, waiting for the moment when winds and clouds would shift; princes, kings, princesses, and outsiders all knew this intent, but only Emperor Wu did not suspect.
translations.idiomatic: He humbled himself to win over scholars, waiting for his moment. Princes, princesses, and outsiders all knew his intent, but only Emperor Wu remained unsuspicious.

sentences.zh: 及長有才學，善屬文。

translations.literal: When he grew up he had talent and learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up he proved talented and learned, skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 武帝御諸子以禮，朝見不甚數。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu governed his sons by ritual propriety and did not summon them to court very often.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu treated his sons with formal propriety and did not summon them to court often.

sentences.zh: 綜恒怨不見知。

translations.literal: Zong constantly resented not being recognized.
translations.idiomatic: Zong constantly resented feeling unrecognized.

sentences.zh: 每出蕃，淑媛恒隨之至鎮。

translations.literal: Whenever he went out to his fief, Lady Wu always followed him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went to his fief, Lady Wu always accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 時年十五，尚裸袒嬉戲於前，晝夜無別。

translations.literal: At the time he was fifteen, yet still played bare-chested before her, making no distinction between day and night.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifteen, yet still played bare-chested before her, making no distinction between day and night.

sentences.zh: 妃袁氏，尚書令昂之女也。

translations.literal: His consort was Lady Yuan, daughter of Minister of Works Ang.
translations.idiomatic: His consort Lady Yuan was the daughter of Minister of Works Ang.

sentences.zh: 淑媛恒節其宿止，遇袁妃尤不以道，內外咸有穢聲。

translations.literal: Lady Wu constantly regulated his lodging arrangements; toward Consort Yuan she was especially improper, and both inside and outside there were scandalous rumors.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu constantly controlled his lodging. Toward Consort Yuan she was especially improper, and scandal spread inside and outside the household.

sentences.zh: 綜後在徐州，政刑酷暴，又有勇力，制及奔馬，暴殺駒犢。

translations.literal: Later, when Zong was in Xuzhou, his governance and punishments were cruel and violent; he also had courage and strength, could keep pace with galloping horses, and wantonly killed foals and calves.
translations.idiomatic: Later in Xuzhou, Zong's rule was cruel and violent. Strong and fearless, he could keep pace with galloping horses and wantonly killed foals and calves.

sentences.zh: 常陰服微行，著烏絲布帽。

translations.literal: He often wore dark clothing and traveled incognito, wearing a black silk cloth cap.
translations.idiomatic: He often traveled incognito in dark clothing and a black silk cap.

sentences.zh: 夜出無有期度，招引道士，探求數術。

translations.literal: He went out at night without fixed schedule, inviting Daoist priests and seeking out numerological arts.
translations.idiomatic: He went out at night without fixed schedule, inviting Daoist priests and pursuing occult arts.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏多通，每武帝有敕疏至，輒忿恚形於顏色。

translations.literal: By nature he was clever, perceptive, and widely learned; whenever an imperial edict or memorial from Emperor Wu arrived, anger would show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and widely learned, he showed anger on his face whenever an edict or memorial arrived from Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 帝性嚴，群臣不敢輕言得失，凡綜所行，弗之知也。

translations.literal: The emperor was stern by nature; ministers and officials did not dare lightly speak of right and wrong, and none of Zong's actions came to his knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stern, and officials dared not speak freely of right and wrong. None of Zong's actions reached his ears.

sentences.zh: 於徐州還，頻裁表陳便宜，求經略邊境。

translations.literal: Upon returning from Xuzhou, he repeatedly submitted memorials proposing practical measures and requesting to manage the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from Xuzhou, he repeatedly submitted memorials proposing practical measures and requesting frontier command.

sentences.zh: 帝並優敕答之。

translations.literal: The emperor each time replied with gracious edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor each time replied with gracious edicts.

sentences.zh: 徐州所有練樹，並令斬殺，以帝小名練故。

translations.literal: All practice trees in Xuzhou he ordered cut down and killed, because the emperor's childhood name was Lian.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered all practice trees in Xuzhou cut down, because the emperor's childhood name was Lian.

sentences.zh: 累致意尚書僕射徐勉，求出鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: He repeatedly conveyed his wishes to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works Xu Mian, requesting to go out and govern Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked Vice Director Xu Mian to help him obtain a posting at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 勉未敢言，因是怒勉，餉以白團扇，圖伐檀之詩，言其賄也。

translations.literal: Mian did not dare speak of it; Zong therefore grew angry at Mian and sent him a white round fan painted with the poem Cutting Sandalwood, implying he had taken bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Mian did not dare speak up. Zong grew angry and sent him a white round fan painted with the poem Cutting Sandalwood, implying he had taken bribes.

sentences.zh: 在西州，於別室歲時設席，祠齊氏七廟。

translations.literal: In Xizhou he set out feasts at the proper seasons in a separate chamber to sacrifice to the seven temples of the Qi house.
translations.idiomatic: In Xizhou he held seasonal feasts in a separate chamber to sacrifice to the seven temples of the Qi dynasty.

sentences.zh: 又累微行至曲阿拜齊明帝陵。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly traveled incognito to Qu'e to pay respects at the tomb of Qi Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly traveled incognito to Qu'e to pay respects at Qi Emperor Ming's tomb.

sentences.zh: 然猶無以自信，聞俗說以生者血瀝死者骨滲，即為父子。

translations.literal: Yet he still could not trust himself; he heard a popular saying that if the blood of the living dripped on the dead person's bone and seeped in, they were father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Still unable to trust himself, he heard a popular saying: if a living person's blood dripped on a dead person's bone and seeped in, they were father and son.

sentences.zh: 綜乃私發齊東昏墓，出其骨，瀝血試之。

translations.literal: Zong therefore secretly opened the tomb of Qi Emperor Donghun, took out the bones, and tested them by dripping blood.
translations.idiomatic: Zong secretly opened Qi Emperor Donghun's tomb, took out the bones, and tested them with his blood.

sentences.zh: 既有征矣，在西州生次男月餘日，潛殺之。

translations.literal: When there was a positive sign, while in Xizhou his second son was born; after a little more than a month he secretly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the test proved positive, he secretly killed his second son in Xizhou, barely a month after the birth.

sentences.zh: 既瘞，夜遣人發取其骨又試之，其酷忍如此。

translations.literal: After burial, he sent men at night to dig up the bones and test them again—such was his cruelty and ruthlessness.
translations.idiomatic: After burial he sent men at night to dig up the bones and test them again—such was his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 每對東宮及諸王辭色不恭遜。

translations.literal: Whenever he faced the Eastern Palace and the various princes, his words and expression were not respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Toward the crown prince and the other princes his words and manner were consistently disrespectful.

sentences.zh: 嘗改歲後，問訊臨川王巨集，出至中合，登宏羊車次遺糞而出。

translations.literal: Once after the New Year, when paying a New Year's visit to Prince of Linchuan Hong, he went out to the central gate, climbed onto Hong's sheep cart, and left droppings before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Once after New Year, while paying a visit to Prince of Linchuan Hong, he climbed onto Hong's sheep cart at the central gate and defecated before leaving.

sentences.zh: 居都下所為多如此者。

translations.literal: While residing in the capital, most of his actions were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: While living in the capital, most of his behavior was of this sort.

sentences.zh: 普通四年，為都督、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Putong he became commander-in-chief and Governor of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong 4 he became commander-in-chief and Governor of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 頗勤於事，而不見賓客。

translations.literal: He was quite diligent in affairs but did not receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: He was diligent in affairs but refused to receive guests.

sentences.zh: 其辭訟則隔簾理之。

translations.literal: When hearing lawsuits he judged them from behind a screen.
translations.idiomatic: He heard lawsuits from behind a screen.

sentences.zh: 方幅出行，垂帷於輿，每雲惡人識其面也。

translations.literal: When traveling in formal array, he hung curtains on his carriage and always said he hated people recognizing his face.
translations.idiomatic: When traveling formally, he hung curtains on his carriage, saying he hated being recognized.

sentences.zh: 初，齊故建安王蕭寶寅在魏，綜求得北來道人釋法鸞使入北通問於寶寅，謂為叔父。

translations.literal: Initially, the former Prince of Jian'an of Qi, Xiao Baoyin, was in Wei; Zong obtained the northern monk Shi Faluan and had him go north to communicate with Baoyin, calling him uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Former Prince of Jian'an of Qi, Xiao Baoyin, was in Wei. Zong found the northern monk Shi Faluan and sent him north to contact Baoyin, whom he called uncle.

sentences.zh: 襄陽人梁話母死，法鸞說綜厚賜之，言終可任使。

translations.literal: Liang Hua of Xiangyang's mother died; Faluan persuaded Zong to reward him generously, saying he could ultimately be entrusted with missions.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Hua of Xiangyang's mother died, Faluan persuaded Zong to reward him generously, saying he would prove useful.

sentences.zh: 綜遺話錢五萬。

translations.literal: Zong sent Hua fifty thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Zong sent Hua fifty thousand in cash.

sentences.zh: 及葬畢，引在左右。

translations.literal: When the burial was complete, he brought him into his personal service.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he kept Hua at his side.

sentences.zh: 法鸞在廣陵，往來通魏尤數，每舍淮陰苗文寵家。

translations.literal: Faluan was in Guangling and traveled back and forth to Wei with especial frequency, each time lodging at the home of Miao Wenchong of Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Faluan was in Guangling and traveled frequently to Wei, usually staying with Miao Wenchong of Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 言文寵於綜，綜引為國常侍。

translations.literal: He spoke of Wenchong to Zong, and Zong brought him in as a regular attendant of the princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Wenchong to Zong, who made him a regular attendant of the princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 六年，魏將元法僧以彭城降，帝使綜都督眾軍，權鎮彭城，並攝徐州府事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Wei general Yuan Faseng surrendered Pengcheng; the emperor had Zong command all armies, provisionally garrison Pengcheng, and also oversee Xuzhou headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, Wei general Yuan Faseng surrendered Pengcheng. The emperor put Zong in command of all armies, with provisional garrison at Pengcheng and oversight of Xuzhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 武帝曉別玄象，知當更有敗軍失將，恐綜為北所擒，手敕綜令拔軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu understood celestial signs and knew there would again be defeated armies and lost generals; fearing Zong would be captured by the north, he personally wrote an edict ordering Zong to withdraw his army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu read the celestial signs and knew more defeats were coming. Fearing Zong would be captured by the northerners, he personally ordered him to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 每使居前，勿在人後。

translations.literal: Each time he ordered him to take the front and not remain behind others.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he ordered him to stay in front and not fall behind.

sentences.zh: 綜恐帝覺，與魏安豐王元延明相持，夜潛與梁話苗文寵三騎開北門，涉汴河，遂奔蕭城。

translations.literal: Zong feared the emperor would notice; while facing off against Wei Prince of Anfeng Yuan Yanming, at night he secretly took Liang Hua and Miao Wenchong, three riders, opened the north gate, crossed the Bian River, and fled to Xiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the emperor would notice, Zong faced off against Wei Prince of Anfeng Yuan Yanming. That night he slipped out with Liang Hua and Miao Wenchong through the north gate, crossed the Bian River, and fled to Xiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 自稱隊主，見延明而拜。

translations.literal: He called himself a squad leader, saw Yanming, and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Calling himself a squad leader, he saw Yanming and bowed.

sentences.zh: 延明坐之，問其名氏，不答，曰：「殿下問人有見識者。」

translations.literal: Yanming seated him and asked his name; he did not answer, saying, "Your Highness should ask someone with discernment."
translations.idiomatic: Yanming seated him and asked his name. He did not answer, saying, "Your Highness should ask someone with discernment."

sentences.zh: 延明召使視之，曰：「豫章王也」。

translations.literal: Yanming summoned someone to look at him, who said, "It is the Prince of Yuzhang."
translations.idiomatic: Yanming summoned someone to look at him. "It is the Prince of Yuzhang," he said.

sentences.zh: 延明喜，下地執其手，答其拜，送於洛陽。

translations.literal: Yanming was pleased, descended from his seat, took his hand, returned his bow, and sent him to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Yanming descended, took his hand, returned his bow, and sent him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及旦，齋內諸合猶閉不開，眾莫知所以，唯見城外魏軍叫曰：「汝豫章王昨夜已來在我軍中。」
