translations.literal: By dawn the various gates within the headquarters were still closed and unopened; no one knew why, until they saw the Wei army outside the city shouting, "Your Prince of Yuzhang came to our army last night."
translations.idiomatic: By dawn the headquarters gates were still closed and no one knew why, until Wei troops outside shouted, "Your Prince of Yuzhang came to our army last night."

sentences.zh: 城中既失王所在，眾軍乃退，不得還者甚眾。

translations.literal: The city having lost track of the prince, the armies withdrew, and very many could not return.
translations.idiomatic: With the prince gone, the armies withdrew, and many never made it back.

sentences.zh: 湘州益陽人任煥常有騅馬，乘之退走。

translations.literal: Ren Huan of Yiyang in Xiangzhou had a piebald horse and rode it in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan of Yiyang in Xiangzhou had a piebald horse and rode it in retreat.

sentences.zh: 煥腳為抄所傷，人馬俱弊，煥於橋下歇，抄復至。

translations.literal: Huan's foot was wounded by raiders; both man and horse were exhausted. Huan rested under a bridge, and the raiders came again.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's foot was wounded by raiders. Man and horse exhausted, he rested under a bridge as the raiders closed in again.

sentences.zh: 煥腳痛不復得上馬，於是向馬泣曰：「騅子，我於此死矣。」

translations.literal: Huan's foot pained him so he could no longer mount; he therefore wept to the horse, saying, "Piebald, I will die here."
translations.idiomatic: Too pained to mount, he wept to the horse, "Piebald, I will die here."

sentences.zh: 馬因跪其前腳，煥乃得上馬，遂免難。

translations.literal: The horse therefore knelt on its forelegs, and Huan was able to mount and thus escape danger.
translations.idiomatic: The horse knelt on its forelegs. Huan mounted and escaped.

sentences.zh: 綜長史江革、太府卿祖恒並為魏軍所禽，武帝聞之驚駭。

translations.literal: Zong's chief administrator Jiang Ge and Director of the Palace Storehouse Zu Heng were both captured by the Wei army; Emperor Wu was shocked upon hearing it.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's chief administrator Jiang Ge and Director of the Palace Storehouse Zu Heng were both captured. Emperor Wu was shocked.

sentences.zh: 綜至魏，位侍中、司空、高平公、丹陽王，梁話、苗文寵並為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Zong reached Wei, he held the posts of Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, Duke of Gaoping, and Prince of Danyang; Liang Hua and Miao Wenchong both became Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei, Zong became Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, Duke of Gaoping, and Prince of Danyang. Liang Hua and Miao Wenchong both became Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 綜改名贊字德文，追服齊東昏斬衰，魏太后及群臣並吊。

translations.literal: Zong changed his name to Zan, styled Dewen, and put on hemp mourning with severed edges for Qi Emperor Donghun; the Wei empress dowager and all officials sent condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Zong changed his name to Zan, styled Dewen, and put on severed-edge mourning for Qi Emperor Donghun. The Wei empress dowager and all officials sent condolences.

sentences.zh: 八月，有司奏削爵土，絕其屬籍，改子直姓悖氏。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the relevant offices memorialized to strip his title and fief, cut him from the clan register, and change his son Zhi's surname to the Bei clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, officials memorialized to strip his title and fief, remove him from the clan register, and change his son Zhi's surname to Bei.

sentences.zh: 未及旬日，有詔復屬籍，封直永新侯。

translations.literal: Before ten days had passed, an edict restored him to the clan register and enfeoffed Zhi as Marquis of Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days an edict restored him to the clan register and enfeoffed Zhi as Marquis of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 久之乃策免吳淑媛，俄遇鴆而卒，有詔復其品秩，諡曰敬，使直主其喪。

translations.literal: After a long time Lady Wu was dismissed by edict; soon she encountered poisoned wine and died. An edict restored her rank and title, posthumously naming her Jing, and had Zhi preside over her funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Lady Wu was dismissed by edict. Soon she was poisoned to death. An edict restored her rank, gave her the posthumous name Jing, and had Zhi preside over her funeral.

sentences.zh: 及蕭寶寅據長安反，綜復去洛陽欲奔之。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin held Chang'an in rebellion, Zong again left Luoyang intending to flee to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin rebelled from Chang'an, Zong left Luoyang intending to join him.

sentences.zh: 魏法，度河橋不得乘馬，綜乘馬而行，橋吏執之送洛陽。

translations.literal: By Wei law one could not ride a horse when crossing the river bridge; Zong rode a horse across, and the bridge official seized him and sent him back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei law forbade riding horses on the river bridge. Zong rode across anyway, and bridge officials seized him and sent him back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 魏孝莊初，歷位司徒、太尉，尚帝姊壽陽長公主。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he successively held the posts of Minister of Education and Grand Commandant, and married the emperor's elder sister, the Princess Long of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wei Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he rose to Minister of Education and Grand Commandant and married the emperor's elder sister, Princess Long of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 陳慶之之至洛也，送綜啟求還。

translations.literal: When Chen Qingzhi reached Luoyang, Zong sent a memorial requesting to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Qingzhi reached Luoyang, Zong sent a memorial asking to return.

sentences.zh: 時吳淑媛尚在，敕使以綜小時衣寄之。

translations.literal: At the time Lady Wu was still alive; an edict ordered that Zong's childhood clothes be sent to her.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu was still alive, and an edict ordered Zong's childhood clothes sent to her.

sentences.zh: 信未達而慶之敗。

translations.literal: The letter had not arrived before Qingzhi was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The letter had not arrived before Qingzhi was defeated.

sentences.zh: 未幾，終於魏。

translations.literal: Before long he died in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in Wei.

sentences.zh: 初，綜在魏不得志，嘗作聽鍾鳴、悲落葉以申其志，當時莫不悲之。

translations.literal: Initially, when Zong was frustrated in Wei, he once composed Listening to the Bell Ring and Grieving over Falling Leaves to express his intent; at the time none were not moved to sorrow by them.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated in Wei, Zong once composed Listening to the Bell Ring and Grieving over Falling Leaves to express his feelings. Everyone who read them was moved to sorrow.

sentences.zh: 後梁人盜其柩來奔，武帝猶以子禮祔葬陵次。

translations.literal: Later a man of Liang stole his coffin and fled back; Emperor Wu still buried him by collateral placement at the mausoleum by the rites due a son.
translations.idiomatic: Later a man of Liang stole his coffin and fled home. Emperor Wu still buried him by the rites due a son, in collateral placement at the mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 直字思方，位晉陵太守，沙州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhi, styled Sifang, held the posts of Administrator of Jinling and Governor of Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, styled Sifang, served as Administrator of Jinling and Governor of Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 南康簡王績字世謹，小字四果，武帝第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince Jian of Nankang Ji, styled Shijin, childhood name Siguo, was Emperor Wu's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Nankang Ji, styled Shijin, childhood name Siguo, was Emperor Wu's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 天監七年，封南康郡王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianjian he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 7 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 十年，為南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he became Governor of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he became Governor of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時年七歲，主者有受貨洗改解書，長史王僧孺弗之覺，績見而詰之，便即首服，眾咸歎其聰警。

translations.literal: At the time he was seven years old; a clerk had taken bribes and altered a dismissal document, which Chief Administrator Wang Sengru did not detect. Ji saw it and questioned him, and the man immediately confessed; all admired his keen intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: He was only seven. A clerk had taken bribes and altered a dismissal document, which Chief Administrator Wang Sengru failed to notice. Ji saw it, questioned the clerk, and the man confessed at once. All admired his sharp intelligence.

sentences.zh: 績寡玩好，少嗜欲，居無僕妾，躬事儉約。

translations.literal: Ji had few diversions, little appetite for pleasure, kept no servants or concubines, and personally practiced thrift.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had few diversions and little appetite for pleasure. He kept no servants or concubines and lived frugally himself.

sentences.zh: 所有租秩，悉寄天府。

translations.literal: All his rent and salary he deposited entirely in the imperial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He deposited all his rent and salary in the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 及薨後，少府有南康國無名錢數千萬。

translations.literal: After his death, the Privy Treasury held several tens of millions in unmarked cash from the Nankang princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the Privy Treasury held tens of millions in unmarked cash from the Nankang establishment.

sentences.zh: 子會理嗣。

translations.literal: His son Huili succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huili succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 會理字長才，少聰慧，好文史。

translations.literal: Huili, styled Changcai, was intelligent from youth and fond of literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: Huili, styled Changcai, was bright from youth and fond of literature and history.

sentences.zh: 年十一而孤，特為武帝所愛，衣服禮秩與正王不殊。

translations.literal: At eleven he was orphaned and was especially beloved by Emperor Wu; his clothing and ceremonial rank were no different from a full prince.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at eleven, he was especially beloved by Emperor Wu. His clothing and ceremonial rank were no different from a full prince's.

sentences.zh: 十五為湘州刺史，多信左右。

translations.literal: At fifteen he became Governor of Xiangzhou and trusted his attendants too much.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he became Governor of Xiangzhou and placed too much trust in his attendants.

sentences.zh: 行事劉納每禁之，會理心不平，證以贓貨，收送建鄴。

translations.literal: Acting Governor Liu Na frequently restrained him; Huili was resentful, fabricated evidence of bribery against him, and had him arrested and sent to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Governor Liu Na frequently restrained him. Resentful, Huili fabricated bribery charges and had him arrested and sent to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 納歎曰：「我一見天子，使汝等知。」

translations.literal: Na sighed and said, "Once I see the Son of Heaven, I will make you all know."
translations.idiomatic: Na sighed, "Once I see the Son of Heaven, you will see."

sentences.zh: 會理厚送資糧，數遣慰喻。

translations.literal: Huili generously sent supplies and repeatedly dispatched envoys to console and reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Huili sent generous supplies and repeatedly dispatched envoys to console him.

sentences.zh: 令心腹于青草湖為盜，殺納百口俱盡。

translations.literal: He ordered his trusted men to become bandits at Qingcao Lake and killed Na's entire household of a hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: He had his trusted men become bandits at Qingcao Lake and killed Na's entire household of a hundred persons.

sentences.zh: 累遷都督、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to commander-in-chief and Governor of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commander-in-chief and Governor of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 太清元年，督眾軍北侵，至彭城，為魏師所敗，退歸本鎮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiqing he commanded all armies in a northern invasion, reaching Pengcheng, but was defeated by Wei forces and retreated to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing 1 he led a northern invasion to Pengcheng, was defeated by Wei forces, and retreated to his post.

sentences.zh: 二年，侯景圍城，會理入援。

translations.literal: In the second year Hou Jing besieged the city; Huili marched in to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, when Hou Jing besieged the capital, Huili marched to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 會北徐州刺史封山侯正表將應其兄正德，外托赴援，實謀襲廣陵。

translations.literal: It happened that Governor of North Xuzhou Marquis of Fengshan Zhengbiao was about to respond to his elder brother Zhengde; outwardly claiming to march to the rescue, he actually plotted to attack Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of North Xuzhou Marquis of Fengshan Zhengbiao was about to join his elder brother Zhengde. Claiming to march to the rescue, he actually planned to attack Guangling.

sentences.zh: 會理擊破之，方得進路。

translations.literal: Huili defeated him and only then obtained a path forward.
translations.idiomatic: Huili defeated him and only then could advance.

sentences.zh: 台城陷，會理歸鎮。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Huili returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Huili returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 侯景遣前臨江太守董紹先以武帝手敕召會理。

translations.literal: Hou Jing dispatched former Administrator of Linjiang Dong Shaoxian with an imperial handwritten order from Emperor Wu to summon Huili.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing sent former Administrator of Linjiang Dong Shaoxian with an imperial handwritten order from Emperor Wu to summon Huili.

sentences.zh: 其僚佐曰：「紹先書豈天子意。」

translations.literal: His staff said, "How can Shaoxian's letter represent the Son of Heaven's intent?"
translations.idiomatic: His staff said, "How can Shaoxian's letter represent the emperor's true intent?"

sentences.zh: 咸勸拒之。

translations.literal: All urged him to refuse.
translations.idiomatic: All urged him to refuse.

sentences.zh: 會理用其典簽范子鸞計，曰：「天子年尊，受制賊虜，今有手敕召我入朝，臣子之心，豈得違背。

translations.literal: Huili adopted the plan of his chief clerk Fan Ziluan, saying, "The Son of Heaven is advanced in years and controlled by the rebel captor; now there is a handwritten order summoning me to court—can the heart of a subject refuse?
translations.idiomatic: Huili followed his chief clerk Fan Ziluan's advice: "The emperor is old and held by the rebel. A handwritten order summons me to court. How can a subject refuse?

sentences.zh: 且處江北，功業難成，不若身赴京都，圖之肘腋。」

translations.literal: Moreover, staying north of the river, great achievements are hard to accomplish; it is better to go in person to the capital and plot from close at hand."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, staying north of the river, great deeds are hard to accomplish. Better to go to the capital in person and act from within."

sentences.zh: 遂納紹先。

translations.literal: Thereupon he admitted Shaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: He admitted Shaoxian.

sentences.zh: 紹先入，以烏幡麾眾，單馬遣之至都。

translations.literal: Shaoxian entered first, waved a black banner to command the troops, and sent Huili alone on horseback to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxian entered first, waved a black banner to command the troops, and sent Huili alone on horseback to the capital.

sentences.zh: 景以為司空兼尚書令。

translations.literal: Hou Jing appointed him Minister of Works concurrently serving as Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing appointed him Minister of Works and concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 雖在寇手，每思匡復，與西鄉侯勸等潛布腹心，要結壯士。

translations.literal: Though in the rebel's hands, he constantly thought of restoring the realm; with Marquis of Xixiang Quan and others he secretly placed trusted men and recruited stalwart warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Though held by the rebel, he constantly plotted restoration. With Marquis of Xixiang Quan and others he secretly placed trusted agents and recruited stalwart warriors.

sentences.zh: 時范陽祖皓斬董紹先，據廣陵城起義，期以會理為內應。

translations.literal: At the time Zu Hao of Fanyang killed Dong Shaoxian, seized Guangling city, and raised a rebellion, planning to use Huili as an inside collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Hao of Fanyang killed Dong Shaoxian, seized Guangling, and rebelled, planning to use Huili as an inside collaborator.

sentences.zh: 皓敗，辭相連及。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, testimony implicated Huili as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was defeated, testimony implicated Huili as well.

sentences.zh: 侯景矯詔免會理官，猶以白衣領尚書令。

translations.literal: Hou Jing forged an edict dismissing Huili from office, yet still had him serve as Director of the Department of State Affairs in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing forged an edict dismissing Huili from office, yet still had him serve as Director of the Department of State Affairs in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 是冬，景往晉熙，都下虛弱，會理復與柳敬禮及北兗州司馬成欽謀之。

translations.literal: That winter Hou Jing went to Jinxi; the capital was weak, and Huili again plotted with Liu Jingli and North Yanzhou Chief Administrator Cheng Qin.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Hou Jing went to Jinxi. With the capital weakened, Huili again plotted with Liu Jingli and North Yanzhou Chief Administrator Cheng Qin.

sentences.zh: 敬禮曰：「舉大事必有所資，今無寸兵，安可以動。」

translations.literal: Jingli said, "To undertake a great enterprise one must have resources; now we have not a single soldier—how can we act?"
translations.idiomatic: Jingli said, "A great enterprise requires resources. We have not a single soldier—how can we act?"

sentences.zh: 會理曰：「湖熟有吾故舊三千餘人，昨來相知，克期響集。

translations.literal: Huili said, "At Hushu I have more than three thousand old associates; yesterday we made contact, and they will assemble on the appointed day.
translations.idiomatic: Huili said, "At Hushu I have more than three thousand old associates. We made contact yesterday, and they will assemble on the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 計賊守兵不過千人，若大兵外攻，吾等內應，直取王偉，事必有成。

translations.literal: I estimate the rebel garrison is no more than a thousand men; if a great army attacks from outside and we respond from within, striking directly at Wang Wei, the affair is sure to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel garrison is no more than a thousand men. If a great army attacks from outside while we respond from within and strike Wang Wei directly, we will succeed.

sentences.zh: 縱景後歸，無能為也。」

translations.literal: Even if Hou Jing returns later, he will be able to do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Even if Hou Jing returns later, he will be powerless."

sentences.zh: 敬禮曰：「善」。

translations.literal: Jingli said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Jingli said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 于時百姓厭賊，咸思用命。

translations.literal: At the time the people were weary of the rebels and all wished to devote themselves to the cause.
translations.idiomatic: The people were weary of the rebels and all wished to devote themselves to the cause.

sentences.zh: 建安侯賁以謀告王偉，偉遂收會理及其弟通理。

translations.literal: Marquis of Jian'an Ben reported the plot to Wang Wei, and Wei thereupon arrested Huili and his younger brother Tongli.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Jian'an Ben reported the plot to Wang Wei, who arrested Huili and his younger brother Tongli.

sentences.zh: 時有錢唐褚冕，會理之舊，亦囚於省，問事之所起，考掠千計，終無所言。

translations.literal: At the time there was Chu Mian of Qiantang, an old associate of Huili, also imprisoned in the ministry; asked whence the affair arose, he was tortured in a thousand ways yet said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Mian of Qiantang, an old associate of Huili, was also imprisoned. Asked about the plot, he was tortured in a thousand ways yet said nothing.

sentences.zh: 會理隔壁聞之，遙曰：「褚郎，卿豈不為吾致此邪，然勿言。」

translations.literal: Huili heard from the next cell and called out, "Master Chu, was it not you who brought this upon me? Yet do not speak."
translations.idiomatic: Huili heard from the next cell and called out, "Master Chu, did you not bring this upon me? Yet say nothing."

sentences.zh: 王偉害會理等，冕竟以不服，偉赦之。

translations.literal: Wang Wei killed Huili and the others; Mian ultimately would not confess, and Wei pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei killed Huili and the others. Mian never confessed, and Wei pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 會理弟通理字仲宣，位太子洗馬，封祈陽侯，至是亦遇害。

translations.literal: Huili's younger brother Tongli, styled Zhongxuan, held the post of Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qiyang; at this time he too was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Huili's younger brother Tongli, styled Zhongxuan, was Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household and Marquis of Qiyang. He too was killed.

sentences.zh: 通理弟乂理字季英。

translations.literal: Tongli's younger brother Yili was styled Jiying.
translations.idiomatic: Tongli's younger brother Yili was styled Jiying.

sentences.zh: 生十旬而簡王薨，至三歲能言，見內人分散，涕泣相送，問其故，或曰：「此簡王宮人喪畢去耳。」

translations.literal: Born at ten weeks Prince Jian died; by three he could speak. Seeing palace women dispersing, weeping as they bade farewell, he asked the reason; someone said, "These are Prince Jian's palace women leaving after mourning is complete."
translations.idiomatic: He was born ten weeks before Prince Jian died. By three he could speak. Seeing palace women dispersing in tears, he asked why. Someone said, "These are Prince Jian's palace women leaving after mourning is complete."

sentences.zh: 乂理便號泣，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: Yili immediately wailed and could not contain his grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yili immediately wailed, overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 諸宮人見之，莫不哀感，為之停者三人。

translations.literal: The palace women who saw this were all moved to sorrow; three stopped to remain.
translations.idiomatic: The palace women who saw this were all moved to sorrow. Three stopped to remain.

sentences.zh: 服闋見武帝，升殿，又悲不自勝，帝為之收涕，謂左右曰：「此兒大必為奇士。」

translations.literal: When mourning ended he saw Emperor Wu; ascending the hall, he again could not contain his grief. The emperor wiped away tears for him and said to those around him, "This child when grown will surely be an extraordinary man."
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he saw Emperor Wu. Ascending the hall, he again could not contain his grief. The emperor wiped away tears and said to his attendants, "This child will surely become an extraordinary man."

sentences.zh: 大同八年，封安樂縣侯。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Datong he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anle County.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 8 he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anle County.

sentences.zh: 乂理慷慨慕立功名，每讀書見忠臣烈士，未嘗不廢卷歎曰：「一生之內，當無愧古人。」

translations.literal: Yili was high-spirited and aspired to establish merit and fame; whenever he read of loyal ministers and martyrs, he never failed to put down the scroll and sigh, saying, "Within one lifetime I must not fall short of the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: Yili was high-spirited and aspired to establish merit and fame. Whenever he read of loyal ministers and martyrs, he put down the scroll and sighed, "In one lifetime I must not fall short of the ancients."

sentences.zh: 博覽多識，有文才。

translations.literal: He read widely and knew much, and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely, knew much, and had literary talent.

sentences.zh: 嘗祭孔文舉墓，並為立碑，制文甚美。

translations.literal: He once sacrificed at the tomb of Kong Wenju and also erected a stele for him; the composition was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: He once sacrificed at Kong Wenju's tomb and erected a stele for him with a very fine inscription.

sentences.zh: 及侯景內寇，乂理聚客赴南兗州，隨兄會理入援。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing invaded from within, Yili gathered clients and went to South Yanzhou, following his elder brother Huili to march to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing invaded, Yili gathered clients and went to South Yanzhou, following his elder brother Huili to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，又隨會理還廣陵，因入齊為質乞師。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he again followed Huili back to Guangling and entered Qi as a hostage to request troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he followed Huili back to Guangling and entered Qi as a hostage to request troops.

sentences.zh: 行二日，會景遣董紹先據廣陵，遂追獲之，防嚴不得與兄相見。

translations.literal: After two days' travel, Hou Jing dispatched Dong Shaoxian to seize Guangling; they pursued and captured him, guarding him strictly so he could not see his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: After two days' travel, Hou Jing sent Dong Shaoxian to seize Guangling. They pursued and captured Yili, guarding him so he could not see his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 乃偽請先還都，入辭母，因謂其姊安固主曰：「兄若至，願使善為計自勉，勿顧以為念。

translations.literal: He therefore falsely requested to return to the capital first, entered to bid farewell to his mother, and said to his elder sister the Princess of Angu, "If my elder brother arrives, I hope you will plan well and encourage yourself; do not worry on my account.
translations.idiomatic: He falsely requested to return to the capital first, bid farewell to his mother, and told his elder sister the Princess of Angu, "If my elder brother arrives, plan well and encourage yourself. Do not worry on my account.

sentences.zh: 前途亦思立效，但未知天命何如耳。」

translations.literal: I also wish to achieve merit ahead, but do not yet know what fate holds."
translations.idiomatic: I also wish to achieve merit, but do not yet know what fate holds."

sentences.zh: 至都，以魏降人元貞忠正可以托孤，乃以玉柄扇贈之。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the capital, he regarded the Wei defector Yuan Zhen as loyal and upright and fit to entrust with his orphan, and therefore gave him a jade-handled fan.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the capital, he regarded the Wei defector Yuan Zhen as loyal and upright and fit to entrust with his affairs, and gave him a jade-handled fan.

sentences.zh: 貞怪不受，乂理曰：「後當見憶。」

translations.literal: Zhen, puzzled, would not accept it; Yili said, "You will remember this later."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, puzzled, refused. Yili said, "You will remember this later."

sentences.zh: 會祖皓起兵，乂理奔長蘆，為景所害。

translations.literal: When Zu Hao raised troops, Yili fled to Changlu and was killed by Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Hao rebelled, Yili fled to Changlu and was killed by Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 元貞始悟其前言，往收葬焉。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhen then understood his earlier words and went to recover and bury him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen then understood his earlier words and went to recover and bury him.

sentences.zh: 廬陵威王續字世欣，武帝第五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Wei of Luling Xu, styled Shixin, was Emperor Wu's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei of Luling Xu, styled Shixin, was Emperor Wu's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 天監八年，封廬陵王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianjian he was enfeoffed as Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 8 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 少英果，膂力絕人，馳射應發命中。

translations.literal: From youth he was heroic and resolute, his physical strength unmatched among men; in mounted archery he hit the mark as soon as he released the arrow.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was heroic and resolute, with unmatched strength. In mounted archery he hit the mark as soon as he released the arrow.

sentences.zh: 武帝歎曰：「此我之任城也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu sighed and said, "This is my Rencheng."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sighed, "This is my Rencheng."

sentences.zh: 嘗馳射於帝前，續中兩獐，冠于諸人。

translations.literal: Once, shooting on horseback before the emperor, Xu hit two roe deer, ranking first among all present.
translations.idiomatic: Once, shooting on horseback before the emperor, Xu hit two roe deer, ranking first among all present.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 中大通二年，為都督、雍州刺史、甯蠻校尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong he became commander-in-chief, Governor of Yongzhou, and Commandant Who Pacifies the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong 2 he became commander-in-chief, Governor of Yongzhou, and Commandant Who Pacifies the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 大同元年，遷江州刺史，又為驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he was transferred to Governor of Jiangzhou, and also became General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 1 he became Governor of Jiangzhou, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 又為都督、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He again became commander-in-chief and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again became commander-in-chief and Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司空，諡曰威。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded Minister of Works, posthumously named Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously awarded Minister of Works with the posthumous name Wei.

sentences.zh: 始元帝母阮修容得幸，由丁貴嬪之力，故元帝與簡文相得，而與廬陵王少相狎，長相謗。

translations.literal: Initially Emperor Yuan's mother Lady Ruan gained favor through Noble Consort Ding's efforts; therefore Emperor Yuan and Emperor Jianwen were close, while with Prince of Luling they were intimate in youth but slandered each other when grown.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan's mother Lady Ruan gained favor through Noble Consort Ding's efforts. Emperor Yuan and Emperor Jianwen were close, but he and Prince of Luling were intimate in youth and slandered each other when grown.

sentences.zh: 元帝之臨荊州，有宮人李桃兒者，以才慧得進，及還，以李氏行。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan went to Jingzhou, there was a palace woman named Li Tao'er who advanced through talent and intelligence; when he returned, he took Lady Li with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan went to Jingzhou, a palace woman named Li Tao'er won favor through talent and intelligence. When he returned, he took Lady Li with him.

sentences.zh: 時行宮戶禁重，續具狀以聞。

translations.literal: At the time travel restrictions on palace households were strict; Xu submitted a full report informing the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Travel restrictions on palace households were strict at the time. Xu submitted a full report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 元帝泣對使訴于簡文，簡文和之得止。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan wept as he addressed the envoy and appealed to Emperor Jianwen, who reconciled the matter and had it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan wept as he appealed to Emperor Jianwen through the envoy. Jianwen reconciled the matter and had it stopped.

sentences.zh: 元帝猶懼，送李氏還荊州，世所謂西歸內人者。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan was still afraid and sent Lady Li back to Jingzhou—the person later called "the inner woman who returned west."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was still afraid and sent Lady Li back to Jingzhou—the woman later known as "the inner woman who returned west."

sentences.zh: 自是二王書問不通。

translations.literal: From then on the two princes' correspondence ceased.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the two princes stopped corresponding.

sentences.zh: 及續薨，元帝時為江州，聞問，入合而躍，屧為之破。

translations.literal: When Xu died, Emperor Yuan was then in Jiangzhou; upon hearing the news, he entered his chamber and leaped, breaking his sandals.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu died, Emperor Yuan was in Jiangzhou. Upon hearing the news, he entered his chamber and leaped, breaking his sandals.

sentences.zh: 尋自江州復為荊州，荊州人迎於我境，帝數而遣之，吏人失望。

translations.literal: Soon after, transferred from Jiangzhou back to Jingzhou, the people of Jingzhou came to welcome him at the border; the emperor rebuked and sent them away, and officials and people were disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon transferred from Jiangzhou back to Jingzhou, he found the people of Jingzhou waiting at the border to welcome him. The emperor rebuked and sent them away, and officials and people were disappointed.

sentences.zh: 續多聚馬仗，蓄養趫雄，耽色愛財，極意收斂，倉儲庫藏盈溢。

translations.literal: Xu amassed horses and weapons, kept and trained fierce warriors, indulged in women and loved wealth, and gathered possessions to the utmost; storehouses and treasuries overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu amassed horses and weapons, kept fierce warriors, indulged in women and loved wealth, and gathered possessions until storehouses and treasuries overflowed.

sentences.zh: 臨終有啟，遣中錄事參軍謝宣融送所上金銀器千餘件，武帝始知其富。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he submitted a memorial, dispatching Central Recording Army Adjutant Xie Xuanrong to deliver more than a thousand pieces of gold and silver vessels he had presented; only then did Emperor Wu learn of his wealth.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he submitted a memorial, sending Central Recording Army Adjutant Xie Xuanrong to deliver more than a thousand pieces of gold and silver vessels. Only then did Emperor Wu learn of his wealth.

sentences.zh: 以為財多德寡，因問宣融曰：「王金盡於此乎？」

translations.literal: Thinking wealth great but virtue small, he therefore asked Xuanrong, "Is the prince's gold all here?"
translations.idiomatic: Thinking the prince rich in wealth but poor in virtue, he asked Xuanrong, "Is the prince's gold all here?"

sentences.zh: 宣融曰：「此之謂多，安可加也。

translations.literal: Xuanrong said, "If this is called much, how could there be more?
translations.idiomatic: Xuanrong said, "If this is called much, how could there be more?

sentences.zh: 夫王之過如日月之蝕，欲令陛下知之，故終而不隱。」

translations.literal: A prince's faults are like an eclipse of the sun and moon; wishing Your Majesty to know, he therefore did not conceal them to the end."
translations.idiomatic: A prince's faults are like an eclipse of the sun and moon. Wishing Your Majesty to know, he did not conceal them to the end."

sentences.zh: 帝意乃解。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was then relieved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind was then relieved.

sentences.zh: 世子憑以罪前誅死，次子應嗣。

translations.literal: The heir Ping was previously executed for a crime; the second son Ying succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Ping had been executed for a crime; the second son Ying succeeded.

sentences.zh: 應不慧，王薨，至內庫閱珍物，見金鋌，問左右曰：「此可食不？」

translations.literal: Ying was not intelligent; when the prince died, he went to the inner treasury to inspect precious objects, saw gold ingots, and asked those around him, "Can these be eaten?"
translations.idiomatic: Ying was not intelligent. When the prince died, he went to the inner treasury and saw gold ingots. He asked his attendants, "Can these be eaten?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「不可。」

translations.literal: They answered, "No."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "No."

sentences.zh: 應曰：「既不可食，並特乞汝。」

translations.literal: Ying said, "Since they cannot be eaten, I specially give them all to you."
translations.idiomatic: Ying said, "Since they cannot be eaten, I give them all to you."

sentences.zh: 他皆此類。

translations.literal: Other matters were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Other matters were all of this sort.

sentences.zh: 邵陵攜王綸字世調，小字六真，武帝第六子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xi of Shaoling Lun, styled Shidiao, childhood name Liuzhen, was Emperor Wu's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Shaoling Lun, styled Shidiao, childhood name Liuzhen, was Emperor Wu's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 少聰穎，博學善屬文，尤工尺牘。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and perceptive, broadly learned and skilled at literary composition, especially adept at letters.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was clever and perceptive, broadly learned and skilled at composition, especially adept at letters.

sentences.zh: 天監十三年，封邵陵郡王。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianjian he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shaoling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 13 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 中大通四年，為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong he became Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong 4 he became Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 綸素驕縱，欲盛器服，遣人就巿賒買錦采絲布數百疋，擬與左右職局防合為絳衫、內人帳幔。

translations.literal: Lun was by nature arrogant and unrestrained; wishing to lavish his vessels and apparel, he sent men to the market on credit to buy several hundred bolts of brocade, colored silk, and cloth, planning with his attendants and office staff to make crimson shirts and inner-chamber curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was arrogant and unrestrained by nature. Wishing to lavish his vessels and apparel, he sent men to buy on credit several hundred bolts of brocade and silk to make crimson shirts and inner-chamber curtains.

sentences.zh: 百姓並關閉邸店不出。

translations.literal: The common people all closed their shops and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Shopkeepers all closed their shops and refused to sell.

sentences.zh: 台續使少府巿采，經時不能得，敕責，府丞何智通具以聞，因被責還第。

translations.literal: The court repeatedly sent the Privy Treasury to purchase in the market but for a long time could obtain nothing; an edict rebuked them. Assistant Director He Zhitong reported everything fully and was rebuked and sent back to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: The court repeatedly sent the Privy Treasury to purchase in the market but could obtain nothing for a long time. An edict rebuked them. Assistant Director He Zhitong reported everything and was rebuked and sent home.

sentences.zh: 恒遣心腹馬容戴子高、戴瓜、李撤、趙智英等於路尋目智通，于白馬巷逢之，以槊刺之，刃出於背。

translations.literal: Lun constantly sent trusted men Ma Rong, Dai Zigao, Dai Gua, Li Che, Zhao Zhiying, and others to watch for Zhitong on the road; in White Horse Lane they encountered him and stabbed him with a spear, the blade emerging from his back.
translations.idiomatic: Lun sent trusted men including Ma Rong, Dai Zigao, Dai Gua, Li Che, and Zhao Zhiying to watch for Zhitong. In White Horse Lane they stabbed him with a spear, the blade emerging from his back.

sentences.zh: 智通以血書壁作「邵陵」字乃絕，遂知之。

translations.literal: Zhitong wrote the characters "Shaoling" on the wall in blood before dying, and thus it became known.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitong wrote "Shaoling" on the wall in blood before dying, and thus it became known.

sentences.zh: 帝懸錢百萬購賊，有西州游軍將宋鵲子條姓名以啟，敕遣舍人諸曇粲領齋仗五百人圍綸第，于內人檻中禽瓜、撤、智英。

translations.literal: The emperor posted a reward of a million cash for the assassins; a Western Province patrol general named Song Quezi listed the names in a report. An edict dispatched Palace Attendant Zhu Tancan leading five hundred armed guards to surround Lun's residence, capturing Gua, Che, and Zhiying in the inner women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor posted a reward of a million cash. A Western Province patrol general named Song Quezi named the assassins. An edict sent Palace Attendant Zhu Tancan with five hundred armed guards to surround Lun's residence and capture Gua, Che, and Zhiying in the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 子高驍勇，踰牆突圍，遂免。

translations.literal: Zigao was fierce and brave; he leaped over the wall and broke through the encirclement, thus escaping.
translations.idiomatic: Zigao was fierce and brave. He leaped over the wall, broke through the encirclement, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 智通子敞之割炙食之，即載出新亭，四面火炙之焦熟，敞車載錢設鹽蒜，雇百姓食撤一臠，賞錢一千。

translations.literal: Zhitong's son Changzhi cut off flesh and ate it, then had Che loaded out to Xinting, roasted on all sides over fire until charred; Changzhi's cart carried cash and set out salt and garlic, hiring commoners to eat a slice of Che's flesh for a reward of a thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitong's son Changzhi cut off flesh and ate it, then had Che taken to Xinting and roasted on all sides until charred. Changzhi's cart carried cash and salt and garlic, hiring commoners to eat a slice of Che's flesh for a thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 徒黨並母肉遂盡。

translations.literal: The accomplices' flesh, including their mothers', was thus entirely consumed.
translations.idiomatic: The accomplices' flesh, including their mothers', was entirely consumed.

sentences.zh: 綸鎖在第，舍人諸曇粲並主帥領仗身守視。

translations.literal: Lun was locked in his residence; Palace Attendant Zhu Tancan and the commanders led armed guards to watch over him.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was locked in his residence. Palace Attendant Zhu Tancan and commanders led armed guards to watch over him.

sentences.zh: 免為庶人。

translations.literal: He was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: He was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 經三旬乃脫鎖，頃之復封爵。

translations.literal: After thirty days the shackles were removed; soon after his title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: After thirty days the shackles were removed. Soon after his title was restored.

sentences.zh: 後預餞衡州刺史元慶和，於座賦詩十二韻，末云：「方同廣川國，寂寞久無聲」。

translations.literal: Later, attending the farewell banquet for Governor of Hengzhou Yuan Qinghe, he composed a poem of twelve rhymes at the table, ending with: "Just like the state of Guangchuan, long silent and without renown."
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the farewell banquet for Governor of Hengzhou Yuan Qinghe, he composed a twelve-rhyme poem ending with: "Just like the state of Guangchuan, long silent and without renown."

sentences.zh: 大為武帝賞，曰：「汝人才如此，何慮無聲。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu greatly admired it and said, "With talent like yours, why worry about lacking renown?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu greatly admired it and said, "With talent like yours, why worry about lacking renown?"

sentences.zh: 旬日間，拜郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Within ten days he was appointed Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he was appointed Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，位中衛將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he held the posts of General of the Central Guard and Grand Master with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing 2 he became General of the Central Guard and Grand Master with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 侯景構逆，加征討大都督，率眾討景。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing plotted rebellion, he was additionally appointed Grand Commander for Punitive Campaigns and led troops to attack Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, he was additionally appointed Grand Commander for Punitive Campaigns and led troops against him.

sentences.zh: 將發，帝誡曰：「侯景小豎，頗習行陣，未可以一戰即殄，當以歲月圖之。」

translations.literal: As he was about to set out, the emperor admonished him, saying, "Hou Jing is a petty upstart who is quite practiced in battle formations; he cannot be destroyed in a single engagement—you must plan over months and years."
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to set out, the emperor admonished him: "Hou Jing is a petty upstart practiced in battle. He cannot be destroyed in a single engagement—you must plan over months and years."

sentences.zh: 綸發白下，中江而浪起，有物蕩舟將覆，識者尤異之。

translations.literal: Lun set out from Baixia; mid-river waves rose, something rocked the boat nearly capsizing it—those who understood omens found it especially strange.
translations.idiomatic: Lun set out from Baixia. Mid-river waves rose and something rocked the boat nearly capsizing it—those who understood omens found it especially strange.

sentences.zh: 及次鍾離，景已度採石，綸乃晝夜兼道，旋軍入赴。

translations.literal: When he reached Zhongli, Hou Jing had already crossed Caishi; Lun then traveled day and night by forced marches, wheeling his army about to enter the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Zhongli, Hou Jing had already crossed Caishi. Lun then marched day and night, wheeling his army about to enter the rescue.

sentences.zh: 濟江，中流風起，人馬溺者十一二。

translations.literal: Crossing the river, a wind arose midstream and ten or twenty percent of men and horses drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the river, a wind arose midstream and ten or twenty percent of men and horses drowned.

sentences.zh: 遂率西豐公大春、新淦公大成等步騎三萬發京口，將軍趙伯超請從徑路直指鍾山，出其不意，綸從之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led Duke of Xifeng Dachun, Duke of Xingan Dacheng, and others with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry departing from Jingkou; General Zhao Bochao requested to take the direct route straight to Zhong Mountain and strike by surprise, and Lun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He led Duke of Xifeng Dachun, Duke of Xingan Dacheng, and others with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry from Jingkou. General Zhao Bochao requested the direct route to Zhong Mountain for a surprise strike, and Lun agreed.

sentences.zh: 眾軍奄至，賊徒大駭，分為三道攻綸，綸大破之。

translations.literal: The armies suddenly arrived; the rebel troops were greatly alarmed, divided into three routes to attack Lun, and Lun routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: The armies suddenly arrived. The rebel troops were greatly alarmed, divided into three routes to attack Lun, and Lun routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 翌日，賊又來攻，日晚賊稍退。

translations.literal: The next day the rebels attacked again; toward evening they gradually withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels attacked again. Toward evening they gradually withdrew.

sentences.zh: 南安侯駿以數十騎馳之，賊回拒駿，駿部亂，賊因逼大軍，大軍潰。

translations.literal: Marquis of Nan'an Jun charged with several dozen horsemen; the rebels turned to repel Jun, Jun's unit fell into disorder, and the rebels therefore pressed the main army, which collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Nan'an Jun charged with several dozen horsemen. The rebels turned to repel him, his unit fell into disorder, and the rebels pressed the main army, which collapsed.

sentences.zh: 綸至鍾山戰敗，奔還京口。

translations.literal: Lun was defeated at Zhong Mountain and fled back to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was defeated at Zhong Mountain and fled back to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 軍主霍俊見獲，賊送於城下，逼雲已禽邵陵王。

translations.literal: Army commander Huo Jun was captured; the rebels brought him below the city wall and forced him to say the Prince of Shaoling had been taken.
translations.idiomatic: Army commander Huo Jun was captured. The rebels brought him below the city wall and forced him to say the Prince of Shaoling had been taken.

sentences.zh: 俊偽許之，乃曰：「王小失利，政為糧盡還京口。

translations.literal: Jun falsely agreed and then said, "The prince suffered a small setback and is merely returning to Jingkou because provisions are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Jun falsely agreed and said, "The prince suffered a small setback and is merely returning to Jingkou because provisions are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 俊為托邏所獲，非軍敗也。」

translations.literal: Jun was captured by a patrol—this is not an army defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Jun was captured by a patrol—that is not an army defeat."

sentences.zh: 賊以刀背驅其髀，俊色不變，賊義而舍之。

translations.literal: The rebels struck his thigh with the flat of a blade; Jun's expression did not change, and the rebels, admiring his integrity, released him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels struck his thigh with the flat of a blade. Jun's expression did not change, and the rebels, admiring his integrity, released him.

sentences.zh: 俊，中書舍人靈超子也。

translations.literal: Jun was the son of Palace Secretary Lingchao.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was the son of Palace Secretary Lingchao.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，綸與東揚州刺史大連等入援至驃騎洲，進位司空。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Lun with Governor of East Yangzhou Dalian and others marched to the rescue as far as Piaoqi Isle and was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 3, Lun with Governor of East Yangzhou Dalian and others marched to the rescue as far as Piaoqi Isle and was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 台城陷，綸奔禹穴，東土皆附。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Lun fled to Yu's Cave, and the eastern lands all rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Lun fled to Yu's Cave, and the eastern lands all rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 臨城公大連懼將害己，乃圖之。

translations.literal: Duke of Lincheng Dalian, fearing he would be harmed, therefore plotted against him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Lincheng Dalian, fearing Lun would kill him, plotted against him.

sentences.zh: 綸覺乃去。

translations.literal: Lun detected it and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Lun detected the plot and left.

sentences.zh: 至尋陽，尋陽公大心欲以州讓之，不受。

translations.literal: When he reached Xunyang, Duke of Xunyang Daxin wished to yield the province to him, but he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At Xunyang, Duke of Xunyang Daxin offered to yield the province, but Lun refused.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年，綸至郢州，刺史南平王恪讓州於綸，綸不受。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao, Lun reached Yingzhou; Governor Prince of Nanping Ke wished to yield the province to Lun, but Lun would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In Dabao 1, Lun reached Yingzhou. Governor Prince of Nanping Ke offered to yield the province, but Lun refused.

sentences.zh: 乃上綸為假黃鉞、都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: They thereupon promoted Lun to provisional yellow battle-axe and commander-in-chief of all armies within and without.
translations.idiomatic: They promoted Lun to provisional yellow battle-axe and commander-in-chief of all armies within and without.

sentences.zh: 綸於是置百官，改聽事為正陽殿，內外齋省悉題署焉。

translations.literal: Lun thereupon established the hundred offices, changed the audience hall to Zhengyang Hall, and labeled all inner and outer chambers and offices.
translations.idiomatic: Lun established a full bureaucracy, renamed the audience hall Zhengyang Hall, and labeled all inner and outer offices.

sentences.zh: 而數有變怪，祭城隍神，將烹牛，有赤蛇繞牛口出。

translations.literal: Yet strange omens repeatedly occurred; when sacrificing to the city god and about to boil an ox, a red snake coiled around the ox's mouth and emerged.
translations.idiomatic: Strange omens repeatedly occurred. When sacrificing to the city god and about to boil an ox, a red snake coiled around the ox's mouth and emerged.

sentences.zh: 南浦施安幄帳，無何風起，飄沒于江。

translations.literal: At Nanpu they erected tents and canopies; before long a wind arose and they were blown into the river and lost.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanpu they erected tents and canopies. Before long a wind arose and blew them into the river.

sentences.zh: 于時元帝圍河東王譽于長沙既久，譽請救於綸，綸欲往救之，為軍糧不繼遂止。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Yuan had long besieged Prince of Hedong Yu at Changsha; Yu requested rescue from Lun, and Lun wished to go to his aid, but because army provisions could not be sustained he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan had long besieged Prince of Hedong Yu at Changsha. Yu asked Lun for rescue, but Lun stopped when army provisions ran short.

sentences.zh: 乃與元帝書曰：「道之斯美，以和為貴，況天時地利不及人和。

translations.literal: He therefore wrote to Emperor Yuan, saying, "The beauty of the Way lies in valuing harmony, all the more since heaven's timing and earth's advantage are less than human accord.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Emperor Yuan: "The beauty of the Way lies in harmony, especially since heaven's timing and earth's advantage matter less than human accord.

sentences.zh: 豈可手足肱支，自相屠害。

translations.literal: How can hands and feet, arms and legs, slaughter one another?
translations.idiomatic: How can hands and feet slaughter one another?

sentences.zh: 即日大敵猶強，天讎未雪。

translations.literal: At present the great enemy is still strong, and heaven's vengeance is not yet avenged.
translations.idiomatic: The great enemy is still strong, and heaven's vengeance is not yet avenged.

sentences.zh: 余爾昆弟，在外三人，如不匡救，安用臣子。

translations.literal: You and I are brothers; three of us are outside—if we do not rescue and aid, of what use are we as subjects?
translations.idiomatic: You and I are brothers, and three of us are outside. If we do not rescue him, of what use are we as subjects?

sentences.zh: 如使逆寇未除，家禍仍構，料今訪古，未或弗亡。

translations.literal: If the rebel invader is not eliminated and domestic calamity continues to arise, judging from present and past inquiry, none have failed to perish.
translations.idiomatic: If the rebel is not eliminated and domestic calamity continues, judging from present and past, none have failed to perish.

sentences.zh: 夫征戰之理，義在克勝。

translations.literal: The principle of campaigning lies in achieving victory by righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of war lies in righteous victory.

sentences.zh: 至於骨肉之戰，愈勝愈酷，捷則非功，敗則有喪，勞兵損義，虧失多矣。

translations.literal: As for battles between kin, the more one wins the more cruel it becomes; victory brings no merit, defeat brings mourning, troops are wearied and righteousness harmed—losses are many.
translations.idiomatic: Battles between kin grow crueler with every victory. Victory brings no merit, defeat brings mourning, troops are wearied and righteousness harmed—the losses are great.

sentences.zh: 侯景之軍所以未窺江外者，政為蕃屏盤固，宗鎮強密。

translations.literal: The reason Hou Jing's army has not yet peered beyond the river is precisely that the frontier screens are firm and the princely garrisons strong and dense.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's army has not yet peered beyond the river precisely because the frontier screens are firm and the princely garrisons strong.

sentences.zh: 若自相魚肉，是謂代景行師，景便不勞兵力，坐致成效，醜徒聞此，何快如之！」

translations.literal: If we devour one another like fish and flesh, this is to campaign on Hou Jing's behalf; he need not exert military force and can achieve success while seated—how the vile bandits would rejoice to hear this!"
translations.idiomatic: If we devour one another, we campaign on Hou Jing's behalf. He need not exert force and can succeed while seated—how the vile bandits would rejoice!"

sentences.zh: 元帝復書，陳譽有罪不可解圍之狀。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan replied, setting forth Yu's guilt and why the siege could not be lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan replied, explaining Yu's guilt and why the siege could not be lifted.

sentences.zh: 綸省書流涕曰：「天下之事，一至於斯！」

translations.literal: Lun read the letter and wept, saying, "Affairs under heaven have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Lun read the letter and wept, "Affairs under heaven have come to this!"

sentences.zh: 左右聞之，莫不掩泣。

translations.literal: Those around him who heard it all covered their faces and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him covered their faces and wept.

sentences.zh: 於是大修器甲，將討侯景。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly repaired weapons and armor, preparing to campaign against Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He greatly repaired weapons and armor, preparing to campaign against Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 元帝聞其盛，乃遣王僧辯帥舟師一萬以逼綸。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, hearing of his strength, dispatched Wang Sengbian leading ten thousand naval troops to press Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of his strength, Emperor Yuan dispatched Wang Sengbian with ten thousand naval troops to press Lun.

sentences.zh: 綸將劉龍武等降僧辯，綸遂與子躓等十餘人輕舟走武昌。

translations.literal: Lun's generals Liu Longwu and others surrendered to Sengbian; Lun then fled with his son Zhi and more than ten others in light boats to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's generals Liu Longwu and others surrendered to Sengbian. Lun fled with his son Zhi and more than ten others in light boats to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 沙門法磬與綸有舊，藏之岩石之下。

translations.literal: The monk Faqing, who had old ties with Lun, hid him beneath the rocks.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Faqing, an old friend of Lun's, hid him beneath the rocks.

sentences.zh: 時綸長史韋質、司馬薑偉先在外，聞綸敗，馳往迎。

translations.literal: At the time Lun's chief administrator Wei Zhi and chief administrator Jiang Wei were outside; hearing of Lun's defeat, they raced to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's chief administrator Wei Zhi and chief administrator Jiang Wei were outside. Hearing of his defeat, they raced to meet him.

sentences.zh: 元帝復遣將徐文盛追攻之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan again dispatched General Xu Wensheng to pursue and attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan again sent General Xu Wensheng to pursue and attack him.

sentences.zh: 綸復收卒屯于齊昌郡，將引魏軍共攻南陽。

translations.literal: Lun again gathered troops and encamped in Qichang Commandery, planning to bring Wei troops to jointly attack Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lun gathered troops and encamped in Qichang Commandery, planning to bring Wei troops to attack Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 侯景將任約襲綸，綸敗走。

translations.literal: Hou Jing's general Ren Yue raided Lun; Lun was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's general Ren Yue raided Lun. Lun was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 定州刺史田龍祖迎綸，綸懼為所執，復歸齊昌。

translations.literal: Governor of Dingzhou Tian Longzu welcomed Lun; Lun feared being seized by him and returned again to Qichang.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Dingzhou Tian Longzu welcomed Lun, but Lun feared capture and returned to Qichang.

sentences.zh: 行收兵至汝南，魏所署汝南城主李素孝者，綸之故吏，開城納之。

translations.literal: As he marched gathering troops to Runan, Li Suxiao, whom Wei had appointed lord of Runan city and who was Lun's former subordinate, opened the city and admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: Marching to Runan, he found Li Suxiao—Wei's appointee as lord of Runan and Lun's former subordinate—who opened the city and admitted him.

sentences.zh: 綸乃修復城池，收集士卒，將攻竟陵。

translations.literal: Lun then repaired the city walls, gathered soldiers, and prepared to attack Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Lun repaired the city walls, gathered soldiers, and prepared to attack Jingling.

sentences.zh: 魏聞之，遣大將楊忠、儀同侯幾通攻破城，執綸，綸不為屈。

translations.literal: Wei heard of this and dispatched Great General Yang Zhong and Colonel of Honor Hou Jitong to storm the city, capture Lun, and Lun would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Wei heard of this and sent Great General Yang Zhong and Colonel of Honor Hou Jitong to storm the city and capture Lun, who would not submit.

sentences.zh: 通乃臥大鼓，使綸坐上殺之，投於江岸，經日色不變，鳥獸莫敢近。

translations.literal: Jitong then laid a great drum on its side, had Lun sit upon it and killed him, and cast him on the riverbank; for a whole day his complexion did not change, and birds and beasts dared not approach.
translations.idiomatic: Jitong laid a great drum on its side, had Lun sit on it and killed him, and cast him on the riverbank. For a whole day his complexion did not change, and birds and beasts dared not approach.

sentences.zh: 時飛雪飄零，屍橫道路，周回數步，獨不沾灑。

translations.literal: At the time flying snow drifted down; corpses lay across the road, yet for several paces around none touched him.
translations.idiomatic: Flying snow drifted down. Corpses lay across the road, yet for several paces around none touched him.

sentences.zh: 舊主帥安陸人郝破敵斂之於襄陽。

translations.literal: His former commander Hao Podi of Anlu gathered his remains at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His former commander Hao Podi of Anlu gathered his remains at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 葬之日，黃雪雰糅，唯塚壙所獨不下雪。

translations.literal: On the day of burial, yellow snow mingled together, yet snow alone did not fall on the tomb mound.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial, yellow snow mingled in the air, yet snow alone did not fall on the tomb mound.

sentences.zh: 楊忠知而悔焉，使乙太牢往祭殯焉。

translations.literal: Yang Zhong learned of it and regretted it, sending a second grand sacrifice to offer rites at the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong learned of it and regretted it, sending a second grand sacrifice to offer rites at the burial.

sentences.zh: 百姓憐之，為立祠廟。

translations.literal: The common people pitied him and built a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: The common people pitied him and built a shrine.

sentences.zh: 岳陽王察遣迎喪，葬于襄陽望楚山南，贈太宰，諡曰安。

translations.literal: Prince of Yueyang Cha sent men to receive the coffin; he was buried south of Wangchu Mountain at Xiangyang, posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor, posthumously named An.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yueyang Cha sent men to receive the coffin. Lun was buried south of Wangchu Mountain at Xiangyang, posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name An.

sentences.zh: 後元帝議追加諡，尚書左丞劉彀議，諡法「怠政交外曰攜」。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Yuan deliberated on adding a posthumous name; Left Assistant Director of the Ministry of Works Liu Gu argued that by posthumous naming law, "neglecting governance and associating with outsiders is called Xi."
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Yuan deliberated on adding a posthumous name. Left Assistant Director Liu Gu argued that by posthumous naming law, "neglecting governance and associating with outsiders is called Xi."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: They followed this.
translations.idiomatic: They followed this.

sentences.zh: 長子堅字長白，大同元年，以例封汝南侯。

translations.literal: The eldest son Jian, styled Changbai; in the first year of Datong, by precedent he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Jian, styled Changbai, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Runan in Datong 1 by precedent.

sentences.zh: 亦善草隸，性頗庸短，嘗與所親書，題云：「嗣王」。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at cursive and clerical script; by nature he was rather mediocre and limited. Once in a letter to a close associate he wrote as heading, "Heir Prince."
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled at cursive and clerical script but rather mediocre by nature. Once in a letter to a close associate he wrote as heading, "Heir Prince."

sentences.zh: 其人得書大駭，執以諫堅，堅曰：「前言戲耳。」

translations.literal: The man who received the letter was greatly alarmed, took it and remonstrated with Jian; Jian said, "What I said before was only in jest."
translations.idiomatic: The recipient was greatly alarmed and remonstrated with Jian. Jian said, "What I said before was only in jest."

sentences.zh: 人曰：「不願以此為戲耳。」

translations.literal: The man said, "I would not wish this to be taken as jest."
translations.idiomatic: The man said, "I would not wish this to be taken as jest."

sentences.zh: 侯景圍城，堅屯太陽門，終日蒱飲，不撫軍政。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing besieged the city, Jian garrisoned Taiyang Gate, drinking and gambling all day, not attending to military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing besieged the city, Jian garrisoned Taiyang Gate, drinking and gambling all day without attending to military affairs.

sentences.zh: 吏士有功，未嘗申理，疫癘所加，亦不存恤，士咸憤怨。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers who achieved merit were never rewarded; those stricken by plague were not cared for; the troops all resented and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers who achieved merit were never rewarded. Those stricken by plague were not cared for. The troops all resented him.

sentences.zh: 太清三年，堅書佐董勳華、白曇朗等以堅私室醞釀，亟有烹宰，不相沾及，忿恨，夜遣賊登樓，城遂陷，堅遇害。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing, Jian's secretarial assistants Dong Xunhua and Bai Tanlang and others, because Jian's private quarters brewed wine and frequently had animals slaughtered without sharing with them, in resentment sent rebels up the tower by night; the city then fell and Jian was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing 3, Jian's secretarial assistants Dong Xunhua and Bai Tanlang and others, resentful that Jian's private quarters brewed wine and slaughtered animals without sharing, sent rebels up the tower by night. The city fell and Jian was killed.

sentences.zh: 弟確。

translations.literal: The younger brother Que.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Que.

sentences.zh: 確字仲正，少驍勇，有文才，尤工楷隸，公家碑碣皆使書之。

translations.literal: Que, styled Zhongzheng; from youth he was fierce and brave, had literary talent, and was especially skilled at regular and clerical script—all public steles and tablets were assigned to him for writing.
translations.idiomatic: Que, styled Zhongzheng, was fierce and brave from youth, talented in letters, and especially skilled at regular and clerical script. All public steles were assigned to him.

sentences.zh: 除秘書丞，武帝謂曰：「為汝能文，所以特有此授。」

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretary Assistant; Emperor Wu said to him, "Because you can write, you are specially given this appointment."
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Secretary Assistant, Emperor Wu told him, "Because you can write, you are specially given this appointment."

sentences.zh: 大同二年，封為正階侯，復徙封永安。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Primary Rank, then transferred to be enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 2 he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Primary Rank, then transferred to Marquis of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 常在第中習騎射，學兵法，時人以為狂。

translations.literal: He constantly practiced mounted archery in his residence and studied military strategy; people of the time thought him mad.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly practiced mounted archery in his residence and studied military strategy. People thought him mad.

sentences.zh: 左右或進諫，確曰：「聽吾為國家破賊，使汝知之。」

translations.literal: When those around him remonstrated, Que said, "Wait until I break the rebels for the state—then you will know."
translations.idiomatic: When those around him remonstrated, Que said, "Wait until I break the rebels for the state—then you will know."

sentences.zh: 鍾山之役，確所向披靡，群賊憚之。

translations.literal: In the battle at Zhong Mountain, Que swept all before him; the rebel bandits feared him.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhong Mountain, Que swept all before him and the rebels feared him.

sentences.zh: 確每臨陣對敵，意甚詳贍，帶甲據鞍，自朝及夕，馳驟往返，不以為勞，諸將服其壯勇。

translations.literal: Whenever Que faced the enemy in battle, his intent was very thorough and generous; armored and in the saddle from morning to evening, he galloped back and forth without considering it labor—all generals admired his bold courage.
translations.idiomatic: In battle Que was thorough and resolute. Armored and in the saddle from morning to evening, he galloped back and forth without tiring. All generals admired his bold courage.

sentences.zh: 軍敗，賊使負炮，不之知也。

translations.literal: When the army was defeated, the rebels had him carry baggage and did not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was defeated, the rebels had him carry baggage and did not recognize him.

sentences.zh: 確因隙自拔，得達朱方。

translations.literal: Que seized an opening to free himself and reached Zhufang.
translations.idiomatic: Que seized an opening to escape and reached Zhufang.

sentences.zh: 及後侯景乞盟，憚確及趙威方在外，慮為後患，啟求召確入城。

translations.literal: Later when Hou Jing requested a truce, fearing Que and Zhao Weifang outside and worrying they would become a later threat, he petitioned requesting Que be summoned into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Hou Jing requested a truce, fearing Que and Zhao Weifang outside, he petitioned to have Que summoned into the city.

sentences.zh: 詔乃召確為南中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Que as General of the Southern Palace Guard and Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Que as General of the Southern Palace Guard and Governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 確知此盟多貳，城必淪沒，欲先遣趙威方入，確因南奔。

translations.literal: Que knew this truce was largely duplicitous and the city would surely fall; he wished first to send Zhao Weifang in while he himself fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Que knew the truce was largely duplicitous and the city would fall. He wished to send Zhao Weifang in while he fled south.

sentences.zh: 綸聞之，逼確使入。

translations.literal: Lun heard of this and forced Que to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Lun heard of this and forced Que to enter.

sentences.zh: 確猶不肯，綸流涕謂曰：「汝欲反邪！」

translations.literal: Que still would not agree; Lun wept and said to him, "Do you wish to rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: Que still refused. Lun wept and said, "Do you wish to rebel?"

sentences.zh: 時台使周石珍在坐，確曰：「侯景雖云欲去，而不解長圍，以意而推，其事可見。

translations.literal: At the time Court Envoy Zhou Shizhen was present; Que said, "Although Hou Jing says he wishes to leave, he does not lift the long siege—judging by intent, the matter is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Court Envoy Zhou Shizhen was present. Que said, "Although Hou Jing says he wishes to leave, he does not lift the long siege. Judging by intent, the matter is clear.

sentences.zh: 今召我入，未見益也。」

translations.literal: Now summoning me in, I see no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Summoning me in now brings no benefit."

sentences.zh: 石珍曰：「敕旨如此，侯豈得辭。」

translations.literal: Shizhen said, "The imperial order is thus—how can the marquis refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen said, "The imperial order is thus—how can the marquis refuse?"

sentences.zh: 確執意猶堅，綸大怒，謂趙伯超曰：「譙州，卿為我斬之。

translations.literal: Que's resolve remained firm; Lun was greatly angered and said to Zhao Bochao, "Qiaozhou, you cut him down for me.
translations.idiomatic: Que remained firm. Lun was furious and said to Zhao Bochao, "Qiaozhou, cut him down for me.

sentences.zh: 當齎首赴闕。」

translations.literal: I will carry the head to the palace."
translations.idiomatic: I will carry the head to the palace."

sentences.zh: 伯超揮刃眄曰：「我識君耳，刀豈識君。」

translations.literal: Bochao waved his blade and glanced aside, saying, "I know you—but would the blade know you?"
translations.idiomatic: Bochao waved his blade and glanced aside. "I know you—but would the blade know you?"

sentences.zh: 確流涕而出，遂入城。

translations.literal: Que wept as he departed and then entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Que wept as he departed and entered the city.

sentences.zh: 及景背盟復圍城，城陷，確排闥入啟。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing broke the truce and again besieged the city, the city fell; Que pushed open the door and entered to report.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing broke the truce and again besieged the city, the city fell. Que pushed open the door to report.

sentences.zh: 時武帝方寢，確曰：「城已陷矣。」

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Wu was just asleep; Que said, "The city has fallen."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was asleep. Que said, "The city has fallen."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「猶可一戰不？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Can we still fight one battle?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Can we still fight one battle?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「人心不可。

translations.literal: He replied, "The people's hearts will not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The people's hearts will not allow it.

sentences.zh: 臣向格戰不禁，縋下僅得至此。」

translations.literal: I fought at the barrier but could not hold; I lowered myself by rope and barely reached here."
translations.idiomatic: I fought at the barrier but could not hold. I lowered myself by rope and barely reached here."

sentences.zh: 武帝歎曰：「自我得之，自我失之，亦復何恨，幸不累子孫。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu sighed and said, "I gained it myself and I lost it myself—what regret is there? Fortunately it does not implicate my descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sighed, "I gained it myself and I lost it myself—what regret is there? Fortunately it does not implicate my descendants."

sentences.zh: 乃使確為慰勞文，謂曰：「爾速去謂汝父，無以二宮為念。」

translations.literal: He then had Que compose a message of consolation, saying to him, "Go quickly and tell your father not to worry about the two palaces."
translations.idiomatic: He had Que compose a message of consolation: "Go quickly and tell your father not to worry about the two palaces."

sentences.zh: 及出見景，景愛其膂力，恒令在左右。

translations.literal: When he went out and saw Hou Jing, Jing admired his physical strength and constantly kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When he went out and saw Hou Jing, Jing admired his strength and kept him at his side.

sentences.zh: 後從景仰見飛鳶，群賊爭射不中，確射之應弦即落。

translations.literal: Later while following Jing he looked up and saw a flying kite; the rebel bandits competed to shoot but missed; Que shot and it fell as the string sounded.
translations.idiomatic: Later while following Jing he saw a flying kite. The rebels competed to shoot but missed. Que shot and it fell as the string sounded.

sentences.zh: 賊徒忿嫉，咸勸除之。

translations.literal: The rebel troops, resentful and jealous, all urged he be eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, resentful and jealous, all urged he be eliminated.

sentences.zh: 先是綸遣典簽唐法隆密導確，確謂使者曰：「侯景輕恌，可一夫力致。

translations.literal: Earlier Lun had sent Chief Clerk Tang Falong to secretly guide Que; Que told the envoy, "Hou Jing is reckless and arrogant—a single man's strength can bring him down.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lun had sent Chief Clerk Tang Falong to secretly guide Que. Que told the envoy, "Hou Jing is reckless and arrogant—a single man's strength can bring him down.

sentences.zh: 確不惜死，欲手刃之。

translations.literal: Que does not begrudge death and wishes to kill him with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: I do not begrudge death and wish to kill him with my own hand.

sentences.zh: 卿還啟家王，願勿以一子為念。」

translations.literal: You return and report to my father the prince—please do not worry on account of one son."
translations.idiomatic: Return and report to my father—please do not worry on account of one son."

sentences.zh: 後與景獵鍾山，同逐禽，引弓將射景，弦斷不得發，賊覺殺之。

translations.literal: Later while hunting at Zhong Mountain with Jing, pursuing game together, he drew his bow intending to shoot Jing; the string broke and he could not release—the rebels detected it and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Later while hunting at Zhong Mountain with Jing, he drew his bow intending to shoot Jing. The string broke and he could not release. The rebels detected it and killed him.

sentences.zh: 武陵王紀字世詢，武帝第八子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Wuling Ji, styled Shixun, was Emperor Wu's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wuling Ji, styled Shixun, was Emperor Wu's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 少而寬和，喜怒不形於色，勤學有文才。

translations.literal: From youth he was generous and gentle; pleasure and anger did not show on his face; he studied diligently and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was generous and gentle. Pleasure and anger never showed on his face. He studied diligently and had literary talent.

sentences.zh: 天監十三年，封武陵王。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianjian he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 13 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 尋授揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 中書詔成，武帝加四句曰：「貞白儉素，是其清也；

translations.literal: When the Secretariat edict was completed, Emperor Wu added four lines, saying, "Upright and plain, frugal and simple—this is his purity;
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat edict was completed, Emperor Wu added four lines: "Upright and plain, frugal and simple—this is his purity;

sentences.zh: 臨財能讓，是其廉也；

translations.literal: facing wealth yet able to yield—this is his integrity;
translations.idiomatic: facing wealth yet able to yield—this is his integrity;

sentences.zh: 知法不犯，是其慎也；

translations.literal: knowing the law yet not violating it—this is his prudence;
translations.idiomatic: knowing the law yet not violating it—this is his prudence;

sentences.zh: 庶事無留，是其勤也。」

translations.literal: handling all affairs without delay—this is his diligence."
translations.idiomatic: handling all affairs without delay—this is his diligence."

sentences.zh: 紀特為帝愛，故先作牧揚州。

translations.literal: Ji was especially beloved by the emperor, and therefore was first made governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was especially beloved by the emperor and was therefore first made governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 大同三年，為都督、益州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong he became commander-in-chief and Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 3 he became commander-in-chief and Governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 以路遠固辭，帝曰：「天下方亂，唯益州可免，故以處汝，汝其勉之。」

translations.literal: Because the road was far he firmly declined; the emperor said, "The realm is now in turmoil; only Yizhou can be spared, and therefore I place you there—exert yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Because the road was far he firmly declined. The emperor said, "The realm is in turmoil. Only Yizhou can be spared, and therefore I place you there. Exert yourself."

sentences.zh: 紀歔欷，既出復入。

translations.literal: Ji sighed and wept; having gone out he returned again.
translations.idiomatic: Ji sighed and wept. Having gone out he returned again.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝嘗言我老，我猶再見汝還益州也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You once said I am old—I shall yet see you again when you return to Yizhou."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You once said I am old—I shall yet see you again when you return to Yizhou."

sentences.zh: 紀在蜀，開建寧、越嶲，貢獻方物，十倍前人。

translations.literal: While in Shu, Ji opened Jianning and Yuexi, presenting tribute goods ten times what his predecessors had offered.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu, Ji opened Jianning and Yuexi and presented tribute ten times what his predecessors had offered.

sentences.zh: 朝嘉其績，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: The court praised his achievements and added the title Grand Master with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his achievements and added the title Grand Master with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 初，天監中，震太陽門，成字曰：「紹宗梁位唯武王。」

translations.literal: Initially, during Tianjian, Taiyang Gate was struck by lightning, forming characters that read, "To continue the Liang lineage, only the Martial King."
translations.idiomatic: During Tianjian, lightning struck Taiyang Gate, forming characters that read, "To continue the Liang lineage, only the Martial King."

sentences.zh: 解者以武陵王當之，於是朝野屬意焉。

translations.literal: Interpreters held that the Prince of Wuling was meant; thereupon court and countryside fixed their hopes on him.
translations.idiomatic: Interpreters held that the Prince of Wuling was meant, and court and countryside fixed their hopes on him.

sentences.zh: 及侯景陷台城，上甲侯韶西上至硤，出武帝密敕，加紀侍中、假黃鉞、都督征討諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、太尉、承制。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing took the capital, Senior Armorer Hou Shao went west to Xia and produced Emperor Wu's secret edict, adding for Ji the posts of Palace Attendant, provisional yellow battle-axe, commander-in-chief of punitive campaigns, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Commandant, and authority to act by imperial mandate.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing took the capital, Senior Armorer Hou Shao went west to Xia with Emperor Wu's secret edict, appointing Ji Palace Attendant, provisional yellow battle-axe, commander-in-chief of punitive campaigns, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Commandant, and authority to act by imperial mandate.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年六月辛酉，紀乃移告諸州征鎮，遣世子圓照領二蜀精兵三萬，受湘東王繹節度。

translations.literal: On the xinyou day of the sixth month of the first year of Dabao, Ji issued notices to the garrisons of all provinces, dispatching his heir Yuanzhao to lead thirty thousand elite troops of the two Shu regions under the command of Prince of Xiangdong Yi.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day of the sixth month of Dabao 1, Ji notified the provincial garrisons and dispatched his heir Yuanzhao with thirty thousand elite Shu troops under Prince of Xiangdong Yi's command.

sentences.zh: 繹命圓照且頓白帝，未許東下。

translations.literal: Yi ordered Yuanzhao to halt at Baidi for the time being and did not permit him to march east.
translations.idiomatic: Yi ordered Yuanzhao to halt at Baidi and did not permit him to march east.

sentences.zh: 七月甲辰，湘東王繹遣鮑檢報紀以武帝崩問。

translations.literal: On the jiachen day of the seventh month, Prince of Xiangdong Yi dispatched Bao Jian to report to Ji the news of Emperor Wu's death.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the seventh month, Prince of Xiangdong Yi sent Bao Jian to report Emperor Wu's death to Ji.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬寅，紀總戎將發益鎮，繹使胡智監至蜀，以書止之曰：「蜀中鬥絕，易動難安，弟可鎮之，吾自當滅賊。」

translations.literal: On the renyin day of the eleventh month, as Ji was about to marshal his army and depart from the Yizhou garrison, Yi sent Hu Zhijian to Shu with a letter stopping him, saying, "Shu is isolated and steep—easy to stir up, hard to stabilize. Younger brother, you can hold it; I myself will destroy the rebels."
