translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day of the eleventh month, as Ji was about to depart from Yizhou, Yi sent Hu Zhijian with a letter stopping him: "Shu is isolated and steep—easy to stir up, hard to stabilize. Younger brother, hold it; I will destroy the rebels myself."

sentences.zh: 又別紙云：「地擬孫、劉，各安境界，情深魯、衛，書信恒通。」

translations.literal: On a separate sheet he wrote, "Our territories may compare to Sun and Liu, each securing his own borders; our affection is deep as Lu and Wei, and letters should constantly pass between us."
translations.idiomatic: On a separate sheet he wrote, "Our territories may compare to Sun and Liu, each securing his own borders. Our affection is deep as Lu and Wei, and letters should constantly pass between us."

sentences.zh: 二年四月乙丑，紀乃僭號於蜀，改年曰天正，暗與蕭棟同名。

translations.literal: On the yichou day of the fourth month of the second year, Ji usurped the imperial title in Shu, changed the era name to Tianzheng, secretly sharing the same character zheng as Xiao Dong.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the fourth month of year 2, Ji usurped the imperial title in Shu, changed the era name to Tianzheng, secretly sharing the character zheng with Xiao Dong.

sentences.zh: 識者尤之，以為于文「天」為二人，「正」為一止，言各一年而止也。

translations.literal: Those with insight blamed this, holding that in the characters "tian" meant two men and "zheng" meant one stop—signifying each would reign one year and stop.
translations.idiomatic: Those with insight blamed this, holding that in the characters tian meant two men and zheng meant one stop—signifying each would reign one year and stop.

sentences.zh: 紀又立子圓照為皇太子，圓正為西陽王，圓滿竟陵王，圓普南譙王，圓肅宜都王。

translations.literal: Ji also established his son Yuanzhao as crown prince, Yuanzheng as Prince of Xiyang, Yuanman as Prince of Jingling, Yuanpu as Prince of Nanqiao, and Yuansu as Prince of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji established his son Yuanzhao as crown prince, Yuanzheng as Prince of Xiyang, Yuanman as Prince of Jingling, Yuanpu as Prince of Nanqiao, and Yuansu as Prince of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 以巴西、梓潼二郡太守永豐侯撝為征西大將軍、益州刺史，封秦郡王。

translations.literal: He appointed Marquis of Yongfeng Hui, Administrator of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong, as Grand General Who Conquers the West and Governor of Yizhou, enfeoffing him as Prince of Qin Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Marquis of Yongfeng Hui, Administrator of Baxi and Zitong, as Grand General Who Conquers the West and Governor of Yizhou, enfeoffing him as Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 司馬王僧略、直兵參軍徐怦並固諫，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Wang Senglue and Direct Troops Adjutant Xu Peng both firmly remonstrated, and all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Wang Senglue and Direct Troops Adjutant Xu Peng both firmly remonstrated and were killed.

sentences.zh: 僧略，僧辯弟；

translations.literal: Senglue was Sengbian's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Senglue was Sengbian's younger brother;

sentences.zh: 怦，勉從子也，以諫，且以怦與將帥書云：「事事往人口具」，以為反於己，誅之。

translations.literal: Peng was Mian's grand-nephew. Because of his remonstrance, and because Peng's letters to generals said, "All matters are reported in detail by the envoy," Ji thought he was turning against him and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Peng was Mian's grand-nephew. Because of his remonstrance, and because Peng's letters to generals said, "All matters are reported in detail by the envoy," Ji thought he was turning against him and executed him.

sentences.zh: 永豐侯撝歎曰：「王不克矣。

translations.literal: Marquis of Yongfeng Hui sighed and said, "The prince will not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Yongfeng Hui sighed, "The prince will not succeed.

sentences.zh: 夫善人國之基也，今乃誅之，不亡何待。」

translations.literal: Good men are the foundation of a state; now he kills them—if he does not perish, what must he wait for?"
translations.idiomatic: Good men are the foundation of a state. Now he kills them—if he does not perish, what must he wait for?"

sentences.zh: 又謂所親曰：「昔桓玄年號大亨，識者為謂'二月了'，而玄之敗實在仲春。

translations.literal: He also said to those close to him, "Formerly Huan Xuan's era name was Great Prosperity; those with insight read it as 'finished in the second month,' and Huan Xuan's defeat indeed came in mid-spring.
translations.idiomatic: He also told those close to him, "Formerly Huan Xuan's era name was Great Prosperity; those with insight read it as 'finished in the second month,' and Huan Xuan's defeat indeed came in mid-spring.

sentences.zh: 今年曰天正，在文為'一止'，其能久乎！」

translations.literal: This year's name is Tianzheng—in the characters it is 'one stop'—how can it last long!"
translations.idiomatic: This year's name is Tianzheng—in the characters it is 'one stop'—how can it last long!"

sentences.zh: 丁卯，元帝遣萬州刺史宋簉襲圓照于白帝，圓照弟圓正時為西陽太守，召至，鎖於省內。

translations.literal: On the dingmao day, Emperor Yuan dispatched Governor of Wanzhou Song Qiao to raid Yuanzhao at Baidi; Yuanzhao's younger brother Yuanzheng was then Administrator of Xiyang, summoned and locked inside the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day, Emperor Yuan sent Governor of Wanzhou Song Qiao to raid Yuanzhao at Baidi. Yuanzheng, then Administrator of Xiyang, was summoned and locked inside the ministry.

sentences.zh: 初，楊幹運求為梁州刺史不得，紀以為潼州刺史。

translations.literal: Initially, Yang Ganyun sought to be Governor of Liangzhou but was not granted it; Ji appointed him Governor of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ganyun sought to be Governor of Liangzhou but was not granted it. Ji appointed him Governor of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊法深求為黎州刺史亦不得，以為沙州刺史。

translations.literal: Yang Fashen sought to be Governor of Lizhou but also was not granted it; he was appointed Governor of Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fashen sought to be Governor of Lizhou but was not granted it. He was appointed Governor of Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 二人皆憾不獲所請，各遣使通西魏。

translations.literal: Both men resented not obtaining what they requested and each sent envoys to communicate with Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Both resented not obtaining what they requested and each sent envoys to Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 及聞魏軍侵蜀，紀遣其將譙淹回軍赴援，魏將尉遲迥逼涪水，楊幹運降之。

translations.literal: When they heard Wei troops were invading Shu, Ji dispatched his general Qiao Yan to turn his army back to the rescue; Wei general Yuchi Tong pressed toward Fu River, and Yang Ganyun surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard Wei troops were invading Shu, Ji sent his general Qiao Yan back to the rescue. Wei general Yuchi Tong pressed toward the Fu River, and Yang Ganyun surrendered.

sentences.zh: 迥即趨成都。

translations.literal: Tong then hastened toward Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Tong then hastened toward Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 五月己巳，紀次西陵，軍容甚盛。

translations.literal: On the jisi day of the fifth month, Ji halted at Xiling; his military array was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day of the fifth month, Ji halted at Xiling with a very imposing military array.

sentences.zh: 元帝命護軍將軍陸法和立二城於峽口，名七勝城，鎖江以斷峽。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan ordered Protector of the Army Lu Fahe to build two cities at the gorge mouth, named Seven Victories Cities, blocking the river to cut off the gorge.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan ordered Protector of the Army Lu Fahe to build two cities at the gorge mouth, named Seven Victories Cities, blocking the river to cut off the gorge.

sentences.zh: 時陸納未平，蜀軍復逼，元帝甚憂。

translations.literal: At the time Lu Na was not yet pacified and Shu troops pressed again; Emperor Yuan was greatly worried.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Na was not yet pacified and Shu troops pressed again. Emperor Yuan was greatly worried.

sentences.zh: 法和告急，旬日相繼。

translations.literal: Fahe reported emergencies, one after another within ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe reported emergencies one after another within ten days.

sentences.zh: 元帝乃拔任約於獄，以為晉安王司馬，撤禁兵以配之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan then pulled Ren Yue from prison, appointed him Chief Administrator to Prince of Jin'an, and assigned palace guard troops to him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan pulled Ren Yue from prison, appointed him Chief Administrator to Prince of Jin'an, and assigned palace guard troops to him.

sentences.zh: 並遣宣猛將軍劉棻共約西赴。

translations.literal: He also dispatched General of Manifest Valor Liu Fen together with Yue westward.
translations.idiomatic: He also dispatched General of Manifest Valor Liu Fen with Yue westward.

sentences.zh: 六月，紀築連城，攻絕鐵鎖。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Ji built linked fortifications and attacked, severing the iron chains.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Ji built linked fortifications and severed the iron chains.

sentences.zh: 元帝復于獄拔謝答仁為步兵校尉，配眾一旅上赴。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan again pulled Xie Daren from prison as Commandant of Foot Soldiers and assigned him one brigade to march upstream.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan again pulled Xie Daren from prison as Commandant of Foot Soldiers and assigned him one brigade to march upstream.

sentences.zh: 紀之將發也，江水可揭，前部不得行。

translations.literal: When Ji was about to set out, the river water could be waded; the vanguard could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji was about to set out, the river was so shallow it could be waded. The vanguard could not advance.

sentences.zh: 及登舟，無雨而水長六尺。

translations.literal: When he boarded his boats, though there was no rain the water rose six chi.
translations.idiomatic: When he boarded his boats, though there was no rain the water rose six chi.

sentences.zh: 劉孝勝喜曰：「殆天贊也。」

translations.literal: Liu Xiaosheng rejoiced and said, "Surely heaven approves."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaosheng rejoiced, "Surely heaven approves."

sentences.zh: 將至峽，有黑龍負舟，其將帥咸謂天助。

translations.literal: As they neared the gorge, a black dragon bore up the boats; the generals all said heaven was helping.
translations.idiomatic: As they neared the gorge, a black dragon bore up the boats. The generals all said heaven was helping.

sentences.zh: 及頓兵日久，頻戰不利，師老糧盡，智力俱殫。

translations.literal: When they halted the army for a long time, battles repeatedly went badly, the troops were weary and provisions exhausted, and both wit and strength were spent.
translations.idiomatic: After halting for a long time, battles repeatedly went badly. The troops were weary, provisions exhausted, and both wit and strength spent.

sentences.zh: 又魏人入劍閣，成都虛弱，憂懣不知所為。

translations.literal: Moreover Wei troops entered Jian'ge; Chengdu was weak, and he was distressed and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Wei troops entered Jian'ge. Chengdu was weak, and he was distressed and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 先是，元帝已平侯景，執所俘馘，頻遣報紀。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Yuan had already pacified Hou Jing and held the captured heads and ears, frequently sending reports to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Yuan had pacified Hou Jing and held the captured heads, frequently sending reports to Ji.

sentences.zh: 世子圓照鎮巴東，留執不遣。

translations.literal: The heir Yuanzhao garrisoned Badong and detained the messengers without forwarding the reports.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Yuanzhao garrisoned Badong and detained the messengers without forwarding the reports.

sentences.zh: 啟紀云：「侯景未平，宜急征討。

translations.literal: He reported to Ji, saying, "Hou Jing is not yet pacified; you should urgently campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to Ji, "Hou Jing is not yet pacified. You should urgently campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 已聞荊鎮為景所滅，疾下大軍。」

translations.literal: I have heard the Jing garrison was destroyed by Jing—hurry down with the great army."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard the Jing garrison was destroyed by Jing—hurry down with the great army."

sentences.zh: 紀謂為實然，故仍率眾沿江急進。

translations.literal: Ji believed it was indeed so and therefore still led his troops rapidly downstream along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Ji believed it and still led his troops rapidly downstream along the river.

sentences.zh: 于路方知侯景已平，便有悔色，召圓照責之。

translations.literal: On the road he then learned Hou Jing was already pacified; his face showed regret, and he summoned Yuanzhao to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he learned Hou Jing was already pacified. His face showed regret, and he summoned Yuanzhao to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 圓照曰：「侯景雖誅，江陵未服，宜速平蕩。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhao said, "Though Hou Jing is executed, Jiangling is not yet subdued—you should quickly pacify and sweep clean."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhao said, "Though Hou Jing is executed, Jiangling is not yet subdued. You should quickly pacify it."

sentences.zh: 紀亦以既居尊位，宣言於眾，敢諫者死。

translations.literal: Ji also, having already taken the exalted position, proclaimed to the masses that whoever dared remonstrate would die.
translations.idiomatic: Having taken the exalted position, Ji proclaimed that whoever dared remonstrate would die.

sentences.zh: 蜀中將卒日夜思歸。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers of Shu day and night longed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers of Shu day and night longed to return home.

sentences.zh: 所署江州刺史王開業進曰：「宜還救根本，更思後圖。」

translations.literal: His appointed Governor of Jiangzhou Wang Kaiye advanced and said, "You should return to rescue the foundation and think of later plans."
translations.idiomatic: His appointed Governor of Jiangzhou Wang Kaiye said, "You should return to rescue the foundation and think of later plans."

sentences.zh: 諸將僉以為然。

translations.literal: All the generals agreed this was right.
translations.idiomatic: All the generals agreed.

sentences.zh: 圓照、劉孝勝獨言不可，紀乃止。

translations.literal: Yuanzhao and Liu Xiaosheng alone said it could not be done, and Ji therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhao and Liu Xiaosheng alone objected, and Ji stopped.

sentences.zh: 既而聞王琳將至，潛遣將軍侯叡傍險出法和後，臨水築壘禦琳及法和。

translations.literal: Soon after, hearing Wang Lin was about to arrive, he secretly dispatched General Hou Rui by a perilous route to get behind Fahe and built ramparts by the water to resist Lin and Fahe.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Wang Lin was about to arrive, he secretly sent General Hou Rui by a perilous route behind Fahe and built ramparts by the water to resist Lin and Fahe.

sentences.zh: 元帝書遺紀，遣光州刺史鄭安中往喻意于紀，許其還蜀，專制崏方。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan wrote to Ji and dispatched Governor of Guangzhou Zheng Anzhong to explain his intent to Ji, promising he could return to Shu and hold sole authority over the Min region.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan wrote to Ji and sent Governor of Guangzhou Zheng Anzhong to explain his intent, promising Ji could return to Shu and hold sole authority over the Min region.

sentences.zh: 紀不從命，報書如家人禮。

translations.literal: Ji did not obey the order and replied in the manner of family correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Ji did not obey and replied in the manner of family correspondence.

sentences.zh: 既而侯叡為任約、謝答仁所破，又陸納平，諸軍並西赴，元帝乃與紀書曰：「甚苦大智！

translations.literal: Soon after, Hou Rui was defeated by Ren Yue and Xie Daren; Lu Na was also pacified; all armies marched west together, and Emperor Yuan then wrote to Ji, saying, "Great suffering, Dazhi!
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hou Rui was defeated by Ren Yue and Xie Daren. Lu Na was pacified. All armies marched west, and Emperor Yuan wrote to Ji: "Great suffering, Dazhi!

sentences.zh: 季月煩暑，流金鑠石，聚蚊成雷，封狐千里。

translations.literal: In the late month's oppressive heat, metal flows and stones melt, gathered mosquitoes become thunder, and foxes range a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In the late month's oppressive heat, metal flows and stones melt, gathered mosquitoes become thunder, and foxes range a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 以茲玉體，辛苦行陣，乃睠西顧，我勞如何。

translations.literal: With this jade body enduring hardship in battle lines, yet turning west in affection—how great my toil.
translations.idiomatic: With this jade body enduring hardship in battle, yet turning west in affection—how great my toil.

sentences.zh: 自獯醜憑陵，羯胡叛換，吾年為一日之長，屬有平亂之功，膺此樂推，事歸當璧。

translations.literal: Since the Xiongnu villain relied on force and the Jie barbarians rebelled and changed sides, I am a day older in years and happened to have merit in pacifying disorder; I received this willing endorsement, and the matter fell to the jade disk.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xiongnu villain relied on force and the Jie barbarians rebelled, I am a day older and happened to have merit in pacifying disorder. I received willing endorsement, and the matter fell to the jade disk.

sentences.zh: 儻遣使乎，良所希也。

translations.literal: If you would send an envoy, that is truly what I hope for.
translations.idiomatic: If you would send an envoy, that is truly what I hope for.

sentences.zh: 如曰不然，於此投筆。

translations.literal: If you say otherwise, I lay down my brush here.
translations.idiomatic: If you say otherwise, I lay down my brush here.

sentences.zh: 友于兄弟，分形共氣，兄肥弟瘦，無復相代之期；

translations.literal: Brothers should be friendly, sharing form and breath; elder brother fat and younger brother thin—no longer any time to take each other's place;
translations.idiomatic: Brothers should be friendly, sharing form and breath. Elder brother fat and younger brother thin—no longer any time to take each other's place;

sentences.zh: 讓棗推梨，長罷歡愉之日。

translations.literal: yielding jujubes and pushing pears—the long days of joy are ended.
translations.idiomatic: yielding jujubes and pushing pears—the long days of joy are ended.

sentences.zh: 上林靜拱，聞四鳥之哀鳴，宣室披圖，嗟萬始之長逝。

translations.literal: In the Upper Park one sits quietly in reverence, hearing the mournful cries of four birds; in the Xuan Chamber one unrolls the map, sighing at the long departure of the myriad beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: In the Upper Park one sits quietly, hearing the mournful cries of four birds. In the Xuan Chamber one unrolls the map, sighing at the long departure of the myriad beginnings.

sentences.zh: 心乎愛矣，書不盡言。」

translations.literal: The heart loves indeed, but writing cannot exhaust the words."
translations.idiomatic: The heart loves indeed, but writing cannot exhaust the words."

sentences.zh: 大智，紀別字也。

translations.literal: Dazhi was Ji's alternate style.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhi was Ji's alternate style.

sentences.zh: 帝又為詩曰：「回首望荊門，驚浪且雷奔，四鳥嗟長別，三聲悲夜猿。」

translations.literal: The emperor also composed a poem, saying, "Turning back to gaze at Jingmen, startled waves thunder and rush; four birds sigh at long parting, three cries mourn the night gibbons."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also composed a poem: "Turning back to gaze at Jingmen, startled waves thunder and rush. Four birds sigh at long parting, three cries mourn the night gibbons."

sentences.zh: 圓正在獄中連句曰：「水長二江急，雲生三峽昏，願貰淮南罪，思報阜陵恩。」

translations.literal: Yuanzheng in prison linked verses, saying, "Waters long, the two rivers swift; clouds rise, the Three Gorges dim. I wish to buy off the Huainan crime and think to repay the Fuling grace."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzheng in prison linked verses: "Waters long, the two rivers swift. Clouds rise, the Three Gorges dim. I wish to buy off the Huainan crime and think to repay the Fuling grace."

sentences.zh: 帝看詩而泣。

translations.literal: The emperor read the poem and wept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the poem and wept.

sentences.zh: 紀頻敗，知不振，遣署度支尚書樂奉業往江陵論和緝之計。

translations.literal: Ji was repeatedly defeated and knew he could not recover; he dispatched Acting Director of the Directorate of Revenue Yue Fengye to Jiangling to discuss plans for peace and reconciliation.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly defeated, Ji knew he could not recover. He sent Acting Director of Revenue Yue Fengye to Jiangling to discuss peace.

sentences.zh: 元帝知紀必破，遂拒而不許，於是兩岸十餘城遂俱降。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan knew Ji would surely be broken and therefore refused and would not agree; thereupon more than ten cities on both banks all surrendered together.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan knew Ji would surely be broken and refused. More than ten cities on both banks all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遊擊將軍樊猛率所領至紀所，紀在船中遶床而走，以金擲猛等曰：「此顧卿送我一見七官，卿必當富貴。」

translations.literal: Raiding General Fan Meng led his command to Ji's position; Ji ran around his bed in the boat and threw gold at Meng and the others, saying, "Take this in exchange for sending me to see the Seventh Officer once—you will surely become rich and honored."
translations.idiomatic: Raiding General Fan Meng reached Ji's position. Ji ran around his bed in the boat and threw gold at Meng, saying, "Take this in exchange for sending me to see the Seventh Officer once—you will surely become rich and honored."

sentences.zh: 猛曰：「天子何由可見。

translations.literal: Meng said, "How could the Son of Heaven be seen?
translations.idiomatic: Meng said, "How could the Son of Heaven be seen?

sentences.zh: 殺足下，此金何之。」

translations.literal: Kill you—where would this gold go?"
translations.idiomatic: Kill you—where would this gold go?"

sentences.zh: 猶不敢逼，圍而守之。

translations.literal: He still did not dare press close but encircled and guarded him.
translations.idiomatic: He still did not dare press close but encircled and guarded him.

sentences.zh: 法和馳啟，上密敕樊猛曰：「生還不成功也。」

translations.literal: Fahe sent an urgent report; the emperor secretly ordered Fan Meng, saying, "Returning alive will not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Fahe sent an urgent report. The emperor secretly ordered Fan Meng, "Returning alive will not succeed."

sentences.zh: 猛率甲士祝文簡、張天成拔刃升舟，猶左右奔擲。

translations.literal: Meng led armored soldiers Zhu Wenjian and Zhang Tiancheng, drew blades and boarded the boat; Ji still ran about throwing things left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Meng led armored soldiers Zhu Wenjian and Zhang Tiancheng, drew blades and boarded the boat. Ji still ran about throwing things.

sentences.zh: 第五子圓滿馳來就父，紀首既落，圓滿軀亦分。

translations.literal: The fifth son Yuanman raced to his father; once Ji's head fell, Yuanman's body was also cut apart.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth son Yuanman raced to his father. Once Ji's head fell, Yuanman's body was also cut apart.

sentences.zh: 法和收太子圓照兄弟三人，問圓照曰：「阿郎何以至此？」

translations.literal: Fahe seized the crown prince Yuanzhao and his three brothers and asked Yuanzhao, "Young master, how did you come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: Fahe seized the crown prince Yuanzhao and his three brothers and asked Yuanzhao, "Young master, how did you come to this?"

sentences.zh: 圓照曰：「失計，願為公作奴。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhao said, "A mistaken plan—I wish to be your slave."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhao said, "A mistaken plan—I wish to be your slave."

sentences.zh: 法和叱遣之。

translations.literal: Fahe shouted and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe shouted and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 圓照字明周，中大同初，為益州東齋郎、宋甯宋興二郡太守。

translations.literal: Yuanzhao, styled Mingzhou; at the beginning of Zhongdatong he was Eastern Attendant of Yizhou and Administrator of the two commanderies of Songning and Songxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhao, styled Mingzhou, was at the beginning of Zhongdatong Eastern Attendant of Yizhou and Administrator of Songning and Songxing.

sentences.zh: 遠鎮諸王世子皆在建鄴質守，帝特愛紀，故遣以副紀。

translations.literal: The heirs of princes at distant posts all remained in Jiankang as hostages; the emperor especially loved Ji and therefore dispatched Yuanzhao to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: The heirs of princes at distant posts all remained in Jiankang as hostages. The emperor especially loved Ji and dispatched Yuanzhao to assist him.

sentences.zh: 紀之構釁，悉其謀也。

translations.literal: Ji's plotting of rebellion was entirely his scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's plotting of rebellion was entirely Yuanzhao's scheme.

sentences.zh: 次弟圓正先見鎖在江陵，及紀既以兵終，元帝使謂曰：「西軍已敗，汝父不知存亡。」

translations.literal: The next younger brother Yuanzheng had earlier been seen locked up in Jiangling; when Ji had already ended by arms, Emperor Yuan sent word saying, "The western army is defeated; your father—I do not know whether he lives or dies."
translations.idiomatic: The next younger brother Yuanzheng had been locked up in Jiangling. When Ji had ended by arms, Emperor Yuan sent word: "The western army is defeated. Your father—I do not know whether he lives or dies."

sentences.zh: 意欲使其自裁。

translations.literal: The intent was to make him take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: The intent was to make him take his own life.

sentences.zh: 而圓正既奉此問，便號哭盡哀。

translations.literal: But Yuanzheng, upon receiving this inquiry, immediately wailed with full grief.
translations.idiomatic: But Yuanzheng, upon receiving this inquiry, immediately wailed with full grief.

sentences.zh: 以禍難之興皆由圓照，於是唯哭世子，言不絕聲。

translations.literal: Because the rise of calamity was all due to Yuanzhao, he therefore wept only for the heir, his words unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Because the calamity was all due to Yuanzhao, he wept only for the heir, his words unceasing.

sentences.zh: 上謂圓正聞問悲感，必應自殺，頻看知不能死，又付廷尉獄。

translations.literal: The emperor thought Yuanzheng, hearing the inquiry and moved to grief, would surely kill himself; repeatedly checking and knowing he could not die, he again handed him over to the Court of Judicature prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Yuanzheng would surely kill himself. Repeatedly checking and finding he would not, he handed him to the Court of Judicature prison.

sentences.zh: 及見圓照曰：「阿兄，何乃亂人骨肉，使酷痛如此。」

translations.literal: When he saw Yuanzhao he said, "Elder brother, why did you disrupt the flesh and bone of kin, causing such cruel pain?"
translations.idiomatic: When he saw Yuanzhao he said, "Elder brother, why did you disrupt the flesh and bone of kin, causing such cruel pain?"

sentences.zh: 圓照更無所言，唯雲計誤。

translations.literal: Yuanzhao had nothing more to say, only that the plan was mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhao had nothing more to say, only that the plan was mistaken.

sentences.zh: 並命絕食於獄，齧臂啖之，十三日死，天下聞而悲之。

translations.literal: Both were ordered to fast in prison; they bit their arms and ate the flesh; on the thirteenth day they died, and all under heaven who heard mourned them.
translations.idiomatic: Both were ordered to fast in prison. They bit their arms and ate the flesh. On the thirteenth day they died, and all under heaven mourned them.

sentences.zh: 圓正字明允，紀第二子。

translations.literal: Yuanzheng, styled Mingyun, was Ji's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzheng, styled Mingyun, was Ji's second son.

sentences.zh: 美風儀，善談論，寬和好施，愛接士人。

translations.literal: Handsome in bearing, skilled in discourse, generous and fond of giving, he loved to receive scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in bearing, skilled in discourse, generous and fond of giving, he loved to receive scholars.

sentences.zh: 封江安侯。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangan.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangan.

sentences.zh: 曆西陽太守，有惠政。

translations.literal: He served as Administrator of Xiyang and had benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Xiyang with benevolent governance.

sentences.zh: 既居上流，人附者甚眾。

translations.literal: Once he held the upper reaches, very many people attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the upper reaches, very many people attached themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 及侯景作逆，圓正收兵眾且一萬，後遂跋扈中流，不從王命。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Yuanzheng gathered troops numbering nearly ten thousand; later he became overbearing midstream and did not obey the royal command.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Yuanzheng gathered nearly ten thousand troops. Later he became overbearing midstream and did not obey the royal command.

sentences.zh: 及景破，復謀入蜀。

translations.literal: When Jing was broken, he again plotted to enter Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was defeated, he again plotted to enter Shu.

sentences.zh: 元帝將圖之，署為平南將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan was about to plot against him and appointed him General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was about to plot against him and appointed him General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 及至弗見，使南平嗣王恪等醉而囚之。

translations.literal: When he arrived and was not received, he had Heir Prince of Nanping Ke and others get him drunk and imprison him.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived and was not received, Heir Prince of Nanping Ke and others got him drunk and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 時紀稱梁王。

translations.literal: At the time Ji styled himself Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ji styled himself Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 及紀敗死，為有司奏請絕紀屬籍，元帝許之，賜姓饕餮氏。

translations.literal: When Ji was defeated and died, the relevant offices memorialized requesting that Ji be cut from the clan register; Emperor Yuan approved and bestowed the surname Taotie.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji was defeated and died, officials memorialized to cut him from the clan register. Emperor Yuan approved and bestowed the surname Taotie.

sentences.zh: 紀最為武帝所愛。

translations.literal: Ji was most beloved by Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was most beloved by Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 武帝諸子罕登公位，唯紀以功業顯著，先啟黃扉。

translations.literal: Among Emperor Wu's sons few reached the rank of duke; only Ji, because his achievements were outstanding, first opened the yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: Among Emperor Wu's sons few reached ducal rank. Only Ji, because his achievements were outstanding, first entered the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 兄邵陵王綸屢以罪黜，心每不平。

translations.literal: His elder brother Prince of Shaoling Lun was repeatedly dismissed for crimes, and his heart was always resentful.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Prince of Shaoling Lun was repeatedly dismissed for crimes, and he always resented it.

sentences.zh: 及聞紀為征西，綸撫枕歎曰：「武陵有何功業，而位乃前我？

translations.literal: When he heard Ji was made General Who Conquers the West, Lun beat his pillow and sighed, saying, "What achievements has the Prince of Wuling, that his rank should be ahead of mine?
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Ji was made General Who Conquers the West, Lun beat his pillow and sighed, "What achievements has the Prince of Wuling, that his rank should be ahead of mine?

sentences.zh: 朝廷憒憒，似不知人。」

translations.literal: The court is muddled and confused, as if it does not know men."
translations.idiomatic: The court is muddled, as if it does not know men."

sentences.zh: 武帝聞之，大怒曰：「武陵有恤人拓境之勳，汝有何績。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu heard of this and was greatly angered, saying, "The Prince of Wuling has merit in caring for people and expanding territory—what achievements have you?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu heard of this and was furious. "The Prince of Wuling has merit in caring for people and expanding territory—what achievements have you?"

sentences.zh: 太清初，帝思之，使善畫者張僧繇至蜀圖其狀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiqing, the emperor missed him and sent the skilled painter Zhang Sengyou to Shu to paint his likeness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiqing, the emperor missed him and sent the skilled painter Zhang Sengyou to Shu to paint his likeness.

sentences.zh: 在蜀十七年，南開寧州、越嶲，西通資陵、吐谷渾。

translations.literal: During seventeen years in Shu, he opened Ningzhou and Yuexi to the south and connected with Ziling and Tuyuhun to the west.
translations.idiomatic: During seventeen years in Shu, he opened Ningzhou and Yuexi to the south and connected with Ziling and Tuyuhun to the west.

sentences.zh: 內修耕桑鹽鐵之功，外通商賈遠方之利，故能殖其財用，器甲殷積。

translations.literal: Internally he developed agriculture, sericulture, salt, and iron; externally he connected with merchants for distant profit; therefore he was able to increase his wealth, and weapons and armor accumulated in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Internally he developed agriculture, sericulture, salt, and iron. Externally he connected with merchants for distant profit. His wealth grew and weapons and armor accumulated in abundance.

sentences.zh: 馬八千匹，上足者置之內廄，開寢殿以通之，日落，輒出步馬。

translations.literal: He had eight thousand horses; the finest he placed in the inner stable, opening the sleeping hall to connect with it, and at sunset he would always go out to exercise the horses.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight thousand horses. The finest he placed in the inner stable, opening the sleeping hall to connect with it. At sunset he always went out to exercise the horses.

sentences.zh: 便騎射，尤工舞矟。

translations.literal: He was adept at mounted archery and especially skilled at spear dancing.
translations.idiomatic: He was adept at mounted archery and especially skilled at spear dancing.

sentences.zh: 九日講武，躬領幢隊。

translations.literal: On the ninth day he held military exercises and personally led the banner companies.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day he held military exercises and personally led the banner companies.

sentences.zh: 及聞國難，謂僚佐曰：「七官文士，豈能匡濟。」

translations.literal: When he heard of the national crisis, he said to his staff, "The Seventh Officer is a literary man—how can he restore order?"
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of the national crisis, he told his staff, "The Seventh Officer is a literary man—how can he restore order?"

sentences.zh: 既東下，黃金一斤為餅，百餅為簉，至有百簉；

translations.literal: Once he marched east, gold was cast in one-jin cakes, a hundred cakes making one bundle, reaching as many as a hundred bundles;
translations.idiomatic: Once he marched east, gold was cast in one-jin cakes, a hundred cakes making one bundle, reaching as many as a hundred bundles;

sentences.zh: 銀五倍之，其他錦罽繒采稱是。

translations.literal: silver five times as much, and other brocades, felts, silks, and colored cloths in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: silver five times as much, and brocades, felts, silks, and colored cloths in proportion.

sentences.zh: 每戰則懸金帛以示將士，終不賞賜。

translations.literal: Before each battle he would hang out gold and silk to show the officers and soldiers, yet in the end never rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: Before each battle he hung out gold and silk to show the troops, yet never rewarded them.

sentences.zh: 甯州刺史陳知祖請散金銀募勇士，不聽，慟哭而去。

translations.literal: Governor of Ningzhou Chen Zhizu requested to distribute gold and silver to recruit brave warriors; Ji would not listen, and Chen wept bitterly and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Ningzhou Chen Zhizu requested to distribute gold and silver to recruit warriors. Ji refused, and Chen wept bitterly and departed.

sentences.zh: 自是人有離心，莫肯為用。

translations.literal: From then on people had divided hearts and none were willing to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the troops lost heart and none were willing to serve him.

sentences.zh: 紀頗學觀占，善風角，亦知不復能濟。

translations.literal: Ji had studied observation and divination and was skilled at wind angles; he also knew he could no longer succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had studied divination and was skilled at wind angles. He also knew he could no longer succeed.

sentences.zh: 瞻望氣色，歎吒天道，椎床聲聞於外。

translations.literal: He gazed at the colors of the sky, sighed and lamented at heaven's way, and the sound of pounding his bed was heard outside.
translations.idiomatic: He gazed at the sky, sighed and lamented at heaven's way, and the sound of pounding his bed was heard outside.

sentences.zh: 有請事者，以疾辭不見。

translations.literal: When anyone requested an audience, he declined on grounds of illness and would not receive them.
translations.idiomatic: When anyone requested an audience, he declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 既死，埋於沙洲，不封無櫬。

translations.literal: After his death he was buried on a sandbar, without a mound and without a coffin.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was buried on a sandbar without a mound or coffin.

sentences.zh: 元帝以劉孝勝付廷尉，尋免之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan handed Liu Xiaosheng over to the Court of Judicature, but soon pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan handed Liu Xiaosheng over to the Court of Judicature but soon pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 初，紀將僭號，祅怪不一，內寢柏殿柱繞節生花，其莖四十有六，靃靡可愛，狀似荷花。

translations.literal: Initially, when Ji was about to usurp the imperial title, strange omens were not uniform; in the inner sleeping hall, cypress pillars at the nodes produced flowers, their stems forty-six in number, graceful and lovely, resembling lotus flowers.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji was about to usurp the imperial title, strange omens appeared. In the inner sleeping hall, cypress pillars at the nodes produced flowers—forty-six stems, graceful and lovely, resembling lotus flowers.

sentences.zh: 識者曰：「王敦祅花，非佳事也。」

translations.literal: Those with insight said, "Wang Dun's demonic flowers were no good omen."
translations.idiomatic: Those with insight said, "Wang Dun's demonic flowers were no good omen."

sentences.zh: 時蜀知星人說紀曰：「官若東下，當用申年，太白出西，從之為利。

translations.literal: At the time a Shu astrologer told Ji, "If Your Highness marches east, you should use the year shen; when the Metal Star appears in the west, following it will be advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: A Shu astrologer told Ji, "If Your Highness marches east, you should use the year shen. When the Metal Star appears in the west, following it will be advantageous.

sentences.zh: 申歲發蜀，酉年入荊，不可失也。」

translations.literal: Depart Shu in the shen year, enter Jing in the you year—this must not be missed."
translations.idiomatic: Depart Shu in the shen year, enter Jing in the you year—this must not be missed."

sentences.zh: 發蜀之歲，太白在西，比及明年，則已東出矣。

translations.literal: In the year he departed Shu, the Metal Star was in the west; by the following year it had already moved east.
translations.idiomatic: In the year he departed Shu, the Metal Star was in the west. By the following year it had already moved east.

sentences.zh: 論曰：甚矣，讒佞之為巧也！

translations.literal: The commentary says: How extreme is the craftiness of slanderers and flatterers!
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: How extreme is the craftiness of slanderers and flatterers!

sentences.zh: 夫言附正直，跡在恭敬，悅目會心，無施不可。

translations.literal: Their words attach to uprightness and integrity, their conduct appears respectful; pleasing to the eye and meeting the heart, there is nothing they cannot apply.
translations.idiomatic: Their words attach to uprightness, their conduct appears respectful. Pleasing to the eye and meeting the heart, there is nothing they cannot apply.

sentences.zh: 至乃離父子，間兄弟，廢楚嫡，疏漢嗣，可為太息，良非一塗。

translations.literal: They can even separate father and son, come between brothers, depose the legitimate heir of Chu, and estrange the successor of Han—enough to make one sigh deeply; this is truly not a single path alone.
translations.idiomatic: They can even separate father and son, come between brothers, depose legitimate heirs, and estrange successors—enough to make one sigh deeply. This is not a single path alone.

sentences.zh: 以昭明之親之賢，梁武帝之愛之信，謗言一及，至死不能自明，況於下此者也。

translations.literal: For one as close and worthy as Zhaoming, as loved and trusted by Emperor Wu of Liang—once slander reached him, he could not clear himself even unto death; how much more for those below this level.
translations.idiomatic: For one as close and worthy as Zhaoming, as loved and trusted by Emperor Wu—once slander reached him, he could not clear himself even unto death. How much more for those below him.

sentences.zh: 綜處秦政之疑，懷負尺之志，肆行狂悖，卒致奔亡。

translations.literal: Zong stood in the suspicion of Qin Zheng, harbored the ambition of Fu Chi, acted wildly and perversely, and ultimately fled to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Zong stood under suspicion like Qin Zheng, harbored the ambition of Fu Chi, acted wildly and perversely, and ultimately fled to ruin.

sentences.zh: 廬陵多財為累，雄心自立，未及騁暴，早沒為幸。

translations.literal: Luling was burdened by excessive wealth, had ambitious intent to stand alone; before he could unleash his violence, early death was fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Luling was burdened by excessive wealth and ambitious intent. Before he could unleash his violence, early death was fortune.

sentences.zh: 南康為政有方，居喪以禮，惜乎早夭，不拯危季。

translations.literal: Nankang governed with method, observed mourning by ritual—alas that he died young and could not rescue the perilous final age.
translations.idiomatic: Nankang governed with method and observed mourning by ritual. Alas that he died young and could not rescue the perilous final age.

sentences.zh: 邵陵少而險躁，人道頓亡，晚致勤王，其殆優矣。

translations.literal: Shaoling from youth was dangerous and impetuous, human decency suddenly lost; in his later years he rallied to aid the throne—this was perhaps his one merit.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoling from youth was dangerous and impetuous, human decency suddenly lost. In his later years he rallied to aid the throne—this was perhaps his one merit.

sentences.zh: 武陵地居勢勝，卒致傾覆，才輕志大，能無及乎。

translations.literal: Wuling held a position of superior terrain and power, yet ultimately met collapse—talent light and ambition great, could he have escaped this?
translations.idiomatic: Wuling held superior terrain and power, yet ultimately collapsed—talent light and ambition great. Could he have escaped this?
